dashashwamedh-ghat.heading: Name, legends and history
dashashwamedh-ghat.body: Besides Brahma's ten horse sacrifices, tradition links the ghat with King Divodasa, and another legend says Kama, god of love, once lived here. The historian K. P. Jayaswal connected the name with the Bhara Shiva Nagas, who performed ten horse sacrifices in the 2nd century CE. The stone ghat was built under the Maratha Peshwas soon after 1735. Towards the end of the 18th century Ahilyabai Holkar built a mansion, Ahilyabai Wada, close by. The southern end of the ghat is known as Sitla Ghat, and the Kashi Vishwanath temple is a short walk inland.

dashashwamedh-ghat.heading: Bathing and worship
dashashwamedh-ghat.body: Pilgrims bathe here at dawn, above all in the month of Magh and in the bright half of Jyeshtha. For pilgrims on the Panchatirthi route, which links five bathing places, it is the second dip. They also visit three lingas named in the Puranas, among them Dashashwamedheshvara and Shulatankeshvara. Bengali families immerse images of Durga here at Dussehra and of Kali at Diwali. Besides the daily evening aarti, special aartis are held on Tuesdays and on religious festivals, and a smaller aarti is held in the early morning.

dashashwamedh-ghat.heading: Who performs the aarti
dashashwamedh-ghat.body: The evening aarti is held by two bodies, the Ganga Seva Nidhi and the Gangotri Seva Samiti. Priests stand on raised platforms facing the river, with conch shells, bells, brass cymbals and lamps, while scholars recite from the Vedas. When the Ganga floods, the Nidhi moves the aarti to higher ground: in 2026 it was held on the roof of its office from 17 August, and returned to the river platform on 20 October, after 64 days. On Dev Deepawali the Nidhi holds a maha aarti; in 2025 it was led by 21 priests, with an Amar Jawan Jyoti lit for soldiers. In 2026 Dev Deepawali falls on 24 November.

dashashwamedh-ghat.heading: Man Mahal next door
dashashwamedh-ghat.body: Close by, Man Mahal at Man Mandir Ghat was built in about 1600 by Raja Man Singh of Amber, a close associate of Akbar. In 1734 Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur added an observatory on its roof, planned to calculate time, prepare lunar and solar calendars and follow the stars and planets. The building is a centrally protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India. In February 2019 a Virtual Experiential Museum, set up by the National Council of Science Museums, opened inside it, with 3D views of the ghats and lanes, classical music, sari weaving, the Ramlila and the story of the Ganga's descent.

assi-ghat.heading: The name and its shrines
assi-ghat.body: According to tradition, the goddess Durga threw away her sword after killing the demons Shumbha and Nishumbha, and where it struck the earth the Assi stream began. The ghat marks the traditional southern boundary of the city, and two lingams are worshipped here. One stands under a peepal tree on the ghat; bathing at dawn and then worshipping it is held to be auspicious. The other, Assi-Sangameshwar, is in a small marble temple just off the ghat. Hindus also believe that Tulsidas died at Assi Ghat.

assi-ghat.heading: Morning and evening on the ghat
assi-ghat.body: Subah-e-Banaras was started in 2014. Besides the aarti, music and yoga, the morning programme includes a Vedic yagya and a tribute to the five elements. After sunset a second, smaller aarti is held. It is quieter than Dashashwamedh's and draws more local families than tour groups. On an ordinary day the ghat holds about 22,500 people; on Dev Deepawali more than 600,000 visitors come. In November 2024 the Ganga Mahotsav, Uttar Pradesh Tourism's festival of music and dance, was held at Assi for the first time.

assi-ghat.heading: Tulsi Ghat and Lolark Kund
assi-ghat.body: A few ghats to the north is Tulsi Ghat, named after Tulsidas, who lived there while writing the Ramcharitmanas. In the month of Kartik (October–November) a Krishna Lila is staged there. It also hosts the Dhrupad Mela, five nights of classical music ending on Mahashivratri; the 52nd edition began on 11 February 2026. Near Tulsi Ghat is Lolark Kund, an old stepwell sacred to the sun as Lolark Aditya, repaired by Rani Ahilyabai in the 18th century. It lies about 15 m below ground, down steep stairs, and the Lolark Shashthi rite is performed here for the birth and welfare of sons.

assi-ghat.heading: Getting there and around
assi-ghat.body: The ghat is on Nagwa Road in the Shivala area, at the southern end of the riverfront. Banaras Hindu University is close by, and its students make up most of the ghat's daily visitors. From Varanasi Cantt station, take a reserved auto or an app cab. Dashashwamedh Ghat is about 2.5 km north along the ghats, a walk of 30–40 minutes. By river, the municipal fare for an Assi–Namo Ghat round trip is ₹345 per person; agree any private boat's fare before you step in.

manikarnika-ghat.heading: The name and the tradition
manikarnika-ghat.body: Manikarnika means, roughly, 'jewel of the ear'. In the Kashi Khanda of the Skanda Purana, Vishnu dug a well here with his discus and filled it with the sweat of long austerities. When Shiva and Parvati came, Shiva's jewelled earring fell into it, and Shiva granted that the place would give moksha to all. Another account says the earring was Parvati's, and a third that it was the goddess Sati's. The tank, the Manikarnika or Chakra-Pushkarini Kund, is still at the ghat, and marble footprints, the Vishnu Charan Paduka, mark where Vishnu is said to have done penance.

manikarnika-ghat.heading: Temples and the ghat's builders
manikarnika-ghat.body: The Tarakeshwar Mahadev temple at the ghat was built in the 18th century under the patronage of Ahilyabai Holkar. Tradition holds that Shiva here gives the taraka mantra to the dead, granting liberation, and many families worship at Tarakeshwar after a cremation. Ahilyabai is also credited with a major renovation of the ghat in 1791, and in 1912 Raja Moti Chand raised the platform above flood level. Nearby, the Ratneshwar Mahadev temple stands partly submerged in the river. The Panchkoshi Parikrama, the pilgrimage round Kashi, begins and ends at Manikarnika.

manikarnika-ghat.heading: How cremations are carried out
manikarnika-ghat.body: Manikarnika and Harishchandra Ghat further south are the city's two great cremation grounds. Dom funeral attendants tend the pyres. They give the chief mourner fire from the ghat's never-extinguished flame to light the pyre, and a fee is paid to them even by families who do not take the fire. Cremations continue in every season. When the Ganga floods, as in July and August 2025, the pyres are lit on rooftops and in the lanes behind the ghat, and mourners have had to wade through waist-deep water to reach them.

manikarnika-ghat.heading: Recent work and festival days
manikarnika-ghat.body: In January 2026 redevelopment work was under way at the ghat; the state government said it was meant to provide basic amenities that the area lacked. The district magistrate said some artworks set in the walls were affected, and the government said all such pieces had been preserved by the Culture Department, to be reinstalled when the work ends. On the day after Rangbhari Ekadashi, before Holi, some groups play 'Masane ki Holi' with ash from the pyres at Manikarnika and Harishchandra. Its organisers say the custom has scriptural roots; the Kashi Vidvat Parishad, a council of Sanskrit scholars, says a cremation ground is not a place for festivities.

namo-ghat.heading: From Khidkiya Ghat to Namo Ghat
namo-ghat.body: Khidkiya means window, and the old ghat opened like a window onto the Ganga. Varanasi Smart City chose it as one of six ghats to rebuild, and the foundation stone was laid in 2018. The work was done in two phases over about 81,000 square metres, funded by the Smart City Mission and the Indian Oil Foundation. The namaste sculptures, the tallest 25 feet high, face the river. They express atithi devo bhava, the idea that a guest is to be honoured like a god.

namo-ghat.heading: Facilities on the riverfront
namo-ghat.body: The ghat was planned for easy access. A ramp leads down to the river for elderly and disabled visitors. The floating jetty has bathing areas and changing rooms, and the floating CNG station for boats was the first of its kind in the country. The open-air theatre seats about 1,000 people. There is also a food court serving Banarasi dishes, a library, a children's play area, space for yoga and walking, a tourist information kiosk, public toilets, drinking water and a car park.

namo-ghat.heading: Events held here
namo-ghat.body: Its open space makes Namo Ghat a venue for large public events. Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened the second Kashi Tamil Sangamam here on 17 December 2023. On Dev Deepawali 2025, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath lit the first lamp of the night at Namo Ghat. The Ganga Mahotsav of 1–4 November 2025 held programmes here and at neighbouring Raj Ghat. In October 2026 the Indian Air Force's Wings Over Ganges air show was staged over the river here, and the ghat was closed to the public on show days.

namo-ghat.heading: Getting there and nearby
namo-ghat.body: Namo Ghat is at the northern end of the riverfront and is the easiest ghat to reach by road: an auto from Varanasi Junction takes about 15–30 minutes. Raj Ghat, next door beside the Malviya Bridge, is where the Varuna meets the Ganga. Excavations there, begun in 1940, found a brick structure dated to the 9th century BCE, and the site is regarded as the oldest part of the city. By river, the municipal fare for an Assi–Namo round trip is ₹345 per person.

panchganga-ghat.heading: Five rivers in tradition
panchganga-ghat.body: Tradition names the five rivers as the Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati, Kirana and Dhutapapa. Only the Ganga can be seen; the other four are believed to join it here unseen. The ghat is worshipped as Panchnad Tirtha and is mentioned in the Matsya Purana. Families come here to perform tarpan and shraddh, rites for their ancestors. The month of Kartik matters most on these steps: bathing in the Ganga and offering lamps here through the month are long-standing customs.

panchganga-ghat.heading: Bindu Madhav temple
panchganga-ghat.body: A stairway from the ghat leads up to the Bindu Madhav temple of Vishnu, one of the Pancha Madhava shrines. According to tradition, Vishnu promised the sage Agnibindu that he would remain here, and the name joins the two. The 17th-century French traveller Tavernier described a large temple here with a jewelled image of Vishnu. That temple was destroyed in 1669. The present shrine, a modest stone hall with a low ceiling, was commissioned in the 19th century by the Maratha ruler Bhavan Rao. It holds a shaligram image of Vishnu flanked by Garuda and Hanuman.

panchganga-ghat.heading: The Hazara lamp-tower and akash-deep
panchganga-ghat.body: On the steps of the Shri Math stands the Hazara, a stone lamp-tower built in 1780 by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore. It is made to hold a thousand lamps at once, and 1,008 are lit on Dev Deepawali, which falls on 24 November in 2026. Through Kartik, from its first day to Kartik Purnima, people raise akash-deep in memory of their ancestors. Sesame-oil lamps are placed in a bamboo basket and pulled up a tall bamboo pole on a rope, and women draw rangoli at the foot of the poles.

panchganga-ghat.heading: Getting there
panchganga-ghat.body: Panchganga lies north of Manikarnika and Scindia Ghats, beyond the usual rowing-boat route from Assi to Manikarnika. Motorboats continue north past it to Raj Ghat and Namo Ghat. On foot, walk north along the river from Manikarnika, or come down through the old-city lanes of Ghasi Tola, near Ratan Phatak, which lead to the Bindu Madhav temple. Cremations take place day and night at Manikarnika on the way; pass quietly and do not photograph the pyres or mourners.

ramnagar-fort.heading: The fort and its museum
ramnagar-fort.body: The fort is built of cream-coloured Chunar sandstone on high ground above flood level, with carved balconies, open courtyards and pavilions. The Ministry of Tourism describes its gateways and pavilions as Mughal in style, and its courtyard has a garden and old cannons. The museum fills the former Durbar Hall, the public audience hall. Maharaja Vibhuti Narain Singh set it up in 1964, and it is run privately by the Maharaja Banaras Vidya Mandir Trust. The royal title was abolished in 1971, but Anant Narayan Singh, known as the Maharaja of Benares, still lives in the fort.

ramnagar-fort.heading: Inside the museum
ramnagar-fort.body: The museum has five galleries: vintage cars and palanquins, textiles, the armoury, personal and decorative objects, and old photographs. Among the palanquins are gold- and silver-brocaded ones shaped like lotus flowers, and there are silver elephant saddles and ivory work. The textiles include kimkhwab silk costumes. The armoury holds swords and old guns, some from Africa, Burma and Japan. The astronomical clock, in the decorative gallery, shows the year, month, week, day and time along with the positions of the sun, moon and planets.

ramnagar-fort.heading: Temples, the Ramlila and other festivals
ramnagar-fort.body: A passage from the museum leads down to the riverside temple of Ved Vyasa, traditionally the author of the Mahabharata; the riverbank is especially beautiful at sunset. The fort also has temples to Durga, Chhinnamasta and a south-facing Hanuman. In Magh (January–February) a festival is held in front of the Vyasa temple. The Ramlila began under Maharaja Udit Narayan Singh in the early 1800s. It opens on Anant Chaturdashi and runs for 31 days, sometimes 30, ending on a full moon, and major episodes have drawn up to 100,000 people. UNESCO inscribed Ramlila on its intangible heritage list in 2008.

ramnagar-fort.heading: Getting there and nearby
ramnagar-fort.body: Ramnagar is about 2 km from Banaras Hindu University by the bridge, roughly ten minutes by road, and the Ministry of Tourism describes the fort as a 30-minute boat ride from the city. In Ramnagar town, Lal Bahadur Shastri's paternal house is now a state-run memorial museum showing his rooms, kitchen and everyday things. It was dedicated to the nation on 27 September 2018. The Ministry of Culture's portal lists it as open from 10:00 to 17:00 every day except Tuesday, with free entry and photography allowed.

bhu-new-vishwanath.heading: How the university began
bhu-new-vishwanath.body: The Viceroy, Lord Hardinge, laid the foundation stone of the main campus on Vasant Panchami, 4 February 1916. The university grew out of the Central Hindu College, which Annie Besant founded in 1898, and was set up under the Banaras Hindu University Act of 1915. The land for the main campus was given by the Kashi Naresh, Prabhu Narayan Singh. The campus covers about 1,370 acres and is laid out roughly as a semicircle. The main gate, Singh Dwar, is named after Maharaja Pateshvari Prashad Singh of Balrampur, whose gift paid for it.

bhu-new-vishwanath.heading: Shri Vishwanath Mandir
bhu-new-vishwanath.body: Madan Mohan Malaviya planned the temple as a replica of the Kashi Vishwanath temple in the old city. Its foundation was laid in March 1931, and the Birla family carried out the work, which took 35 years. Built mainly of marble, the temple rises to about 77 metres. Shiva is worshipped on the ground floor, and Lakshmi Narayan and Durga on the first floor. There are also shrines to Nataraja, Parvati, Ganesha, Panchmukhi Mahadev, Hanuman and Saraswati. The temple is run directly by the university. Mahashivratri, the month of Shravan and Navratri are among the festivals kept here.

bhu-new-vishwanath.heading: Bharat Kala Bhavan museum
bhu-new-vishwanath.body: The university museum began on 1 January 1920 as the Bharatiya Lalit Kala Parishad at Godowlia, founded by Rai Krishnadasa with Malaviya. It took the name Bharat Kala Bhavan in 1929. Jawaharlal Nehru laid the foundation of the present building in 1950 and opened it in 1962. The collection holds more than 100,000 objects, among them coins, manuscripts, bronzes, terracottas and Rajasthani and Pahari miniatures. Its galleries include the Nicholas Roerich Gallery and the Alice Boner Gallery. The Ministry of Culture's museums portal lists it as open Monday to Saturday, 10:30 to 16:30, with tickets of ₹20 for Indian and ₹250 for foreign visitors.

bhu-new-vishwanath.heading: Getting there and what is nearby
bhu-new-vishwanath.body: The campus is about 10 km from the city centre and from Varanasi Junction railway station. Auto-rickshaws, taxis, cycle-rickshaws and city buses all serve it, and Varanasi airport is about 30 km away. The temple stands about 1.7 km inside the campus, south-west of the main gate. Shri Guru Ravidas Janmasthan at Seer Govardhanpur is close to the university. Across the Ganga, Ramnagar Fort is about 2 km from the campus by the bridge, roughly ten minutes by road, so the two fit easily into one day.

durga-kund.heading: The goddess and the temple's story
durga-kund.body: Durga is worshipped here in a fierce yet protective form. By tradition, the central image was not made by human hands but appeared on its own. The temple's origin is linked to a story in the Devi-Bhagavata Purana. A king of Varanasi married his daughter Shashikala to Prince Sudarshan, and rival kings went to war over it. Sudarshan prayed to Durga, who fought for them riding her lion. The king then asked her to protect Varanasi, and the temple was built in that belief. The shrine is also mentioned in the Kashi Khand.

durga-kund.heading: Architecture and what to see
durga-kund.body: The temple is in the North Indian Nagara style. Its spire is made of many small shikharas joined together, rising in tiers, and its five segments are said to stand for the five elements. The building is washed in red ochre, the colour of the goddess's image. Inside are carved stone pillars, images of Lakshmi, Saraswati and Kali, and a havan kund where a fire offering is made every day. Beside the temple lies the stepped Durga Kund, a large rectangular tank that was once connected to the Ganga.

durga-kund.heading: Navratri, Sawan and Nag Panchami
durga-kund.body: The busiest days fall in the two Navratris, in spring and autumn. On the fourth day, when the goddess is worshipped as Kushmanda, crowds come here for darshan. In October 2021 the doors opened at 3:00 after the mangla aarti, the men's queue stretched back to the Tridev temple, and police barricaded the approach roads. In the month of Sawan (July–August) the old Durgakund fair sets up swings in the temple grounds and stalls outside. On Nag Panchami, Vishnu resting on the serpent is recreated in the kund.

durga-kund.heading: Getting there and nearby
durga-kund.body: The temple is on Durgakund–Sankat Mochan Road, near Anand Bagh park, in the Bhelupur area. Tulsi Manas Temple is about 250 m to the south, Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple about 700 m to the south-west, and Banaras Hindu University about 1.3 km to the south. A short walk or e-rickshaw ride links Sankat Mochan and Durga Kund, and coming on from Sankat Mochan around dusk suits an afternoon visit to both.

sankat-mochan.heading: History and daily worship
sankat-mochan.body: Tradition holds that Tulsidas composed much of the Ramcharitmanas at this shrine. The stone image in the inner shrine is attributed to his time, while most of the present buildings date from the mid-20th century, when the city grew south around Banaras Hindu University. Every morning and evening devotees recite the Ramcharitmanas before the main shrine, especially the Sundar Kand. The image is dressed with sindoor and marigold garlands. Devotees offer sweets, flowers and oil lamps and recite the Hanuman Chalisa, and Tuesdays and Saturdays are held to be especially auspicious.

sankat-mochan.heading: The temple grounds
sankat-mochan.body: The temple stands on the bank of the Assi, the small river that gives Assi Ghat its name. Around it lies a semi-wild grove of about eight and a half acres, home to troops of monkeys. Besan laddoos for prasad are sold at shops inside the complex. On 7 March 2006 a bomb exploded in the temple during the aarti. Worshippers helped one another, and worship resumed the next day. A police post now stands inside, and every visitor passes a metal detector and a frisk at the entrance.

sankat-mochan.heading: Hanuman Jayanti and the Sangeet Samaroh
sankat-mochan.body: Hanuman Jayanti, on the full moon of Chaitra, draws large crowds. In 2026 the morning programme included shehnai, a Rudrabhishek and recitation of the Ramcharitmanas, and devotees from Bhikharipur carried flags to the temple in a dhwaj yatra. A few days later comes the Sankat Mochan Sangeet Samaroh. Its 103rd edition ran for six nights, 6–11 April 2026, with about 45 performances starting at 19:30 and continuing through the night. Around 150 artists took part, including 12 Padma award winners. Entry is free, and the artists take no fee. The mahant, Vishwambhar Nath Mishra, plays the pakhawaj.

sankat-mochan.heading: Getting there and nearby
sankat-mochan.body: The temple is on Sankat Mochan Road, near the Assi area and Banaras Hindu University. Tulsi Manas Temple and the Durga temple at Durga Kund are about 700 m to the north-east, so the three are easy to visit together. The temple closes at midday and reopens in the afternoon; one plan is to visit around 17:00 and then walk or take an e-rickshaw to Durga Kund for dusk.

kaal-bhairav.heading: The kotwal in Kashi's tradition
kaal-bhairav.body: Kaal Bhairav is a fierce form of Shiva. According to tradition, Bhairav cut off the fifth head of Brahma, and the head stuck to his hand. The sin of killing a Brahmin followed him until he entered Kashi, where the head fell at Kapal Mochan Tirtha. Freed of the sin, he stayed on, and Vishwanath appointed him kshetrapal, the guardian of the city. The temple is mentioned in the Kashi Khand and the Skanda Purana. Devotees believe that his worship removes fear and gives protection.

kaal-bhairav.heading: Inside the temple
kaal-bhairav.body: The sanctum holds a silver-faced image of Bhairav. Only the decorated face is visible through the doorway; the rest of the figure is draped in cloth. The image wears a garland of skulls, holds a trident and a club of peacock feathers, and sits on a dog, his vehicle. An image of Kshetrapal Bhairav is set on the rear door. Drums, bells and the damru are played during aarti. Devotees offer oil, black sesame and flowers.

kaal-bhairav.heading: Bhairav Ashtami and other festivals
kaal-bhairav.body: Bhairav Ashtami, also called Kalabhairav Jayanti, falls on the eighth day of the waning moon in Margashirsha; in 2026 it is on Tuesday 1 December. On this day the cloth that normally covers the image is removed, so the full figure can be seen, adorned with a garland of silver skulls. Devotees keep an all-night vigil, and a midnight aarti is performed with conches, bells and drums. An eight-day pilgrimage to the city's eight Bhairav shrines ends on this day. Annakut and Mahashivratri are also major festivals here.

kaal-bhairav.heading: Getting there and crowds
kaal-bhairav.body: The temple is in Bhaironath, in the Visheshwarganj area in the northern part of the city, about 3 km from Varanasi Cantt station. From the Kashi Vishwanath Dham it is a short auto-rickshaw ride or walk north through the old city. A shared e-rickshaw from Godowlia normally costs ₹30–40 per person, but on New Year's Day 2025 drivers charged up to ₹100. The lanes fill around New Year: on 28 December 2024 the queue ran about 3 km, in three lines, and police set up 11 duty points around the temple.

tulsi-manas.heading: History and the Ramcharitmanas
tulsi-manas.body: The temple was built in 1964 by the Sureka family of Howrah and opened by Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, then President of India. It is also called Sri Satyanarayan Tulsi Manas Mandir, and a small temple stood on the site before it. The temple is dedicated to Rama. Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi, a form of Hindi, rather than in Sanskrit, and this brought the story of Rama to a far wider audience. Recitations and discussions of his works are held here regularly, so the temple is a place of study as well as worship.

tulsi-manas.heading: What to see inside
tulsi-manas.body: The main shrine holds images of Rama with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman. The building is white marble with a shikhara-style spire. The verses on the walls appear in the poem's own metres: chaupai, doha, chhand and soratha. In the 1980s the scholar Philip Lutgendorf noted that the entire text runs across two levels of the inner walls. Look for the life-size mechanical figure of Tulsidas, which recites the epic from a recording. The temple also has a library of Ramayana literature and a museum of manuscripts and artefacts.

tulsi-manas.heading: Garden, aarti and festivals
tulsi-manas.body: Outside, a landscaped garden surrounds a pond lined with statues, with Shiva at its eastern ghat and Tulsidas on its western bank. Aarti is listed at about 6:00 and 16:00. Rama Navami is the busiest festival, with prayers, bhajans and discourses. In the monsoon month of Sawan (July–August), the old Durgakund Sawan fair fills the neighbourhood. In 2025 about a hundred tableaux of episodes from the lives of Rama and Krishna were set up in the temple grounds for the fair.

tulsi-manas.heading: Getting there and nearby
tulsi-manas.body: The temple stands on Sankat Mochan Road in the Durgakund area. The Durga temple is about 250 m to the north, Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple about 700 m to the south-west, and Banaras Hindu University about 1.3 km to the south. The three temples are close enough to see in one afternoon: Sankat Mochan first, then Tulsi Manas, and finally Durga Kund around dusk.

bharat-mata.heading: The founder and the campus
bharat-mata.body: Babu Shiv Prasad Gupta (1883–1944) was a nationalist from Varanasi. In 1920 he started the Hindi daily Aaj, which supported the freedom struggle. On 10 February 1921, during the Non-cooperation movement, he and Bhagwan Das founded Kashi Vidyapith, which Gandhi inaugurated. The temple stands on that campus, renamed Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith in 1995. It was built while India was under British rule, and it is dedicated to Bharat Mata, Mother India, rather than to a deity.

bharat-mata.heading: The opening in 1936
bharat-mata.body: Gandhi opened the temple in 1936, with Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and Vallabhbhai Patel present. He remarked that it held no statues of gods or goddesses, only a map of India in marble. The Hindi poet Maithili Sharan Gupt wrote a poem for the inauguration, and it is displayed on a board inside the building. The map itself was the work of about 20 craftsmen and sculptors over six years.

bharat-mata.heading: The marble map
bharat-mata.body: The map is assembled from 762 pieces of marble. One inch on it equals about 6.4 miles on the ground, and mountains, plains and seas are shown to scale. It covers undivided India and its neighbours, including Afghanistan, Baluchistan, Burma (now Myanmar) and Ceylon (now Sri Lanka). Mountain ranges, rivers and small islands are all marked. A window at ground level in the basement lets visitors look across the surface and see how the peaks rise above the plains.

bharat-mata.heading: Getting there
bharat-mata.body: The temple is on the Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith campus in Maldahiya. It lies off the usual ghat circuit, so it fits best on the way to or from Varanasi Cantt station. The Cantt–Godowlia ropeway has a station named Kashi Vidyapith near the temple. In late September 2026 the ropeway was still in its final trials and not open to passengers, so check whether it has opened before planning around it.

ravidas-janmasthan.heading: Ravidas and his teaching
ravidas-janmasthan.body: Ravidas was a poet and leather craftsman whom his followers revere as a satguru. His mother is remembered as Mata Kalsi and his father as Santokh Dass. Scholars place his life in the 15th and early 16th centuries, though the dates are uncertain. He turned from worship of God in form to the formless, nirguna, divine, and taught that caste and gender should not divide people. One of his poems describes Begampura, a land without sorrow where all are equal. Several traditions name the Rajput princess Mirabai as his disciple. The Ravidassia scripture, Amritbani Guru Ravidass Ji, collects 240 of his hymns.

ravidas-janmasthan.heading: How the temple was built
ravidas-janmasthan.body: The foundation stone was laid on 14 June 1965, Ashadh Sankranti, by Sant Hari Dass, under the guidance of Sant Sarwan Dass of Dera Sachkhand Ballan. Volunteers did much of the building. A small shrine stood by 1972, and statues of Guru Ravidass and Sant Sarwan Dass were installed in 1974. Kanshi Ram, founder of the Bahujan Samaj Party, installed the gold dome. The state's Kashi portal says the temple holds more than 200 kg of gold. On 29 January 2010 Sant Niranjan Dass of Dera Ballan announced here the formation of the Ravidassia religion.

ravidas-janmasthan.heading: Ravidas Jayanti
ravidas-janmasthan.body: The Jayanti falls on Magh Purnima. Before it, Dera Sachkhand Ballan leads devotees from Jalandhar to Varanasi on special trains; in February 2025 about 3,000 people boarded the Begumpura Express at Jalandhar station. At the temple the celebrations bring kirtan, devotional gatherings and a langar that runs without a break. The temple complex has rooms for pilgrims and space for large gatherings. In 2027 the Jayanti falls on 20 February and marks the 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas.

ravidas-janmasthan.heading: Around the temple
ravidas-janmasthan.body: The monumental Guru Ravidas Gate on the road to the temple was opened by President K. R. Narayanan on 16 July 1998; Kanshi Ram had laid its foundation stone in 1997. On 23 February 2024 the Prime Minister unveiled a new statue of Sant Ravidas in the adjoining Ravidas Park and opened about ₹32 crore of works around the birthplace, including approach roads. A foundation stone was laid the same day for a Sant Ravidas Museum. By the river, Sant Ravidas Ghat, opened in 2009, is the southernmost ghat of the city and has a 25-acre memorial park.

bhelupur-jain.heading: Parshvanath in Jain tradition
bhelupur-jain.body: Jain tradition holds that Parshvanath was born in Varanasi to King Ashvasena and Queen Vamadevi, and places his life in the 9th to 8th century BCE. At 30 he renounced the world. After 84 days of meditation he attained kevala jnana, omniscience, which tradition places under a tree near Benares, though other accounts name Ahichchhatra. He attained nirvana at Shikharji, on Parasnath Hill. Scholars regard him as the earliest Tirthankara who was likely a historical figure. His emblem is the snake, and tradition tells that the serpent god Dharanendra spread a canopy of hoods over him as he meditated.

bhelupur-jain.heading: The temples and their images
bhelupur-jain.body: The complex serves both Digambar and Shwetambar Jains, and it also has a shrine to Parshvanath with the goddess Padmavati. The main image in the Digambar temple is a black stone Parshvanath about 75 cm high, dated to the 9th–11th century. The Shwetambar temple's main image is a white Parshvanath about 60 cm high; both are seated in the lotus posture. During the Shwetambar temple's last renovation a new principal image was installed, and the old one remains on the premises. Footprints associated with Parshvanath are also kept here. The 14th-century Vividha Tirtha Kalpa of Jinaprabha Suri describes this temple.

bhelupur-jain.heading: Festivals and other Jain tirthas in Varanasi
bhelupur-jain.body: The main festival is Parshvanath's Janma Kalyanak on Paush Krishna Dashami; in 2027 that tithi falls on 2 January. Jains count Varanasi as the birthplace of four Tirthankaras, not one. Besides Parshvanath at Bhelupur, Suparshvanath is linked with Bhadaini, Chandraprabha with Chandravati, and Shreyansanath with the Sarnath–Singhpur area. Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, is said to have preached in Varanasi and at Sarnath. Bhelupur itself lies about 5 km from the centre of the city.

gurudwara-guru-ka-bagh.heading: Guru Nanak and Pandit Chatur Das
gurudwara-guru-ka-bagh.body: Sikh tradition remembers Guru Nanak's visit through his dialogue with Pandit Chatur Das, a learned Brahmin of the city. Chatur Das asked what faith the Guru followed, since he carried no saligram stone, wore no tulsi beads or rosary, and bore no sandalwood mark. The Guru answered in song, with Bhai Mardana playing the rebab. He recited the Oankar, a composition in Raag Ramkali Dakhani preserved in the Guru Granth Sahib. Its message is that the Name of God and good deeds matter more than ritual objects. Chatur Das became a disciple, and a sangat formed around him.

gurudwara-guru-ka-bagh.heading: The gurudwara today
gurudwara-guru-ka-bagh.body: According to local tradition, the garden's owner, Pandit Gopal Shastri, became a disciple and dedicated the garden to the Guru, and so it came to be called Guru Bagh. The original garden no longer exists. The present building on Guru Nanak Road went up in the early 1970s. Its sanctum stands at one end of a long rectangular hall, with a wide gallery at mid-height on three sides and arched verandas outside. Kirtan, Paath and langar take place every day. The compound covers about one acre, and a few rooms near the entrance are kept for pilgrims who stay overnight.

gurudwara-guru-ka-bagh.heading: Gurpurab at Guru Ka Bagh
gurudwara-guru-ka-bagh.body: Guru Nanak's Gurpurab, on Kartik Purnima, is the main festival here. In 2026 it falls on 24 November, the same day as Dev Deepawali. Continuous kirtan begins the evening before, and the gurudwara is decorated with lights and flowers. On the day, the programme begins before dawn with Asa di Vaar and kirtan, the Guru Granth Sahib is given a ceremonial welcome, and langar is served without a break.

gurudwara-guru-ka-bagh.heading: Other Sikh sites in Varanasi
gurudwara-guru-ka-bagh.body: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, came to Varanasi in 1666 and stayed for several months at the house of Bhai Kalyan Mall. That house is now Gurudwara Bari Sangat at Nichi Bagh. It keeps two of his cloaks, a pair of his shoes and 17 hukamnamas, letters issued by the Gurus and Mata Sahib Devan. Guru Gobind Singh came as a child in 1670. He later sent five Sikhs to study Sanskrit in Varanasi; they stayed at Chetan Math in Bisheshwarganj, which became a centre of the Nirmala Sikhs.

gurudwara-bari-sangat.heading: Guru Tegh Bahadur's stay
gurudwara-bari-sangat.body: When Guru Tegh Bahadur reached Banaras in 1666, he was received by the sangat led by Bhai Javehari Mall, the local masand. He stayed in the house of Bhai Kalyan Mall, on the site where the gurdwara now stands. Bhai Gurbakhsh, the masand of Jaunpur and a skilled musician, sang kirtan for the Guru and was given a mridang, a drum, as a blessing. The present three-storey building dates from the 1950s. It replaced an earlier one built in 1854 by Maharaja Narinder Singh of Patiala.

gurudwara-bari-sangat.heading: Inside the hall
gurudwara-bari-sangat.body: The sanctum stands at one end of a high-ceilinged rectangular hall on the ground floor, with a wide gallery running round it. Off the hall is the Tap Asthan, the small room where the Guru sat in meditation. A narrow well inside the hall is called Baoli Ganga Pargat. Tradition says that when Bhai Kalyan Mall invited the Guru to bathe in the Ganga on an auspicious day, the Guru asked him to lift a stone, and a spring of river water rose. Its water is still used for drinking, and many believe it can heal.

gurudwara-bari-sangat.heading: Relics and hukamnamas
gurudwara-bari-sangat.body: Glass cupboards in the hall hold two very old pairs of shoes, one worn by Guru Tegh Bahadur and the other by the young Gobind Das, later Guru Gobind Singh. A chola, the long loose gown, once used by Guru Tegh Bahadur is also displayed. The gurdwara has seventeen hukamnamas, letters of instruction addressed to the sangat by Guru Tegh Bahadur, Guru Gobind Singh and Mata Sahib Devan. They are not displayed in the hall; the managing committee keeps them separately in its office. Together with the relics, they are the main reason the sangat is counted as the oldest and most important in the city.

gurudwara-bari-sangat.heading: Other Sikh sites in Varanasi
gurudwara-bari-sangat.body: Gurdwara Guru Ka Bagh, on Guru Nanak Road, marks the garden where Guru Nanak arrived on Shivaratri in 1507 and spoke with the pandit Chatur Das. Its present building dates from the 500th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak, marked on 23 November 1969, and it is open from 05:00 to 22:30. Gurdwara Chhoti Sangat recalls another old sangat visited by Guru Tegh Bahadur and Guru Gobind Singh. Sangat Mir Ghat, near the Vishalakshi temple by the river, is sacred to both Gurus. Shri Chetan Math in Bisheshwarganj housed the five Sikhs whom Guru Gobind Singh sent to study Sanskrit.

st-marys-church.heading: A garrison church
st-marys-church.body: St Mary's was paid for by voluntary subscriptions from local residents, after a merchant had held prayer meetings in his home. It was completed in 1812 and consecrated in 1824. It first served the British soldiers stationed in the Cantonment, which is why it is also called the Garrison Church, and the English Church for its tradition of English-language worship. In 1947 it was handed to the Diocese of Lucknow and is now part of the Church of North India. The diocese calls it probably the oldest Protestant church in north India outside Calcutta.

st-marys-church.heading: The building and its grounds
st-marys-church.body: The church is built in a European, Greco-Roman style, with a portico of Doric columns, a triumphal arch and stained-glass windows. Inside, the floor is carved, and its 'peacock carpet' is one of the features visitors remark on. The compound covers 11.25 acres, and the sale of mangoes from its trees helps pay for upkeep. The church stands where The Mall meets Stranger Road in the Cantonment. A December 2024 report described the building as attractive and well kept despite its age.

st-marys-church.heading: Daniel Corrie and worship today
st-marys-church.body: Daniel Corrie reached Calcutta as a chaplain in 1806 and served at posts in the north-western provinces, among them Chunar. He became Archdeacon of Calcutta in 1823 and the first Bishop of Madras in 1835, and died at Madras in 1837. In its early years a chaplain led Matins and Evensong here on Sundays for the soldiers and British residents. Today a small congregation, which the diocese puts at five to fifteen people, keeps Sunday worship going with its own contributions. At Christmas the church is hung with lights, carols are sung, and Anglo-Indian families and other visitors come.

chunar-fort.heading: Legends and early history
chunar-fort.body: Local tradition links the name to Vishnu's Vamana avatar: his first step fell on this hill, called Charanadri, later shortened to Chunar. Another tradition says King Vikramaditya of Ujjain built a house here for his brother Bhartrihari, who had become an ascetic. In the written record, many soldiers of Babur's garrison were killed here in 1529, and their tombs are still venerated. After Sher Shah died in 1545, the Sur rulers held the fort. In 1556 Adil Shah handed it to his minister Hemu, who launched campaigns from Chunar and captured Delhi. Akbar took the fort in 1575.

chunar-fort.heading: What to see inside the walls
chunar-fort.body: The Sonwa Mandap, dated to 1538, has 28 pillars in Hindu style and once served as a gatehouse; the samadhi of Bhartrihari lies behind it. The baoli, or step well, is about 5 m across and nearly 61 m deep, and its water is linked to the Ganga. The west gate carries the fort's only inscriptions, dated 1586, which credit its building under Akbar. Inside are a bungalow associated with Warren Hastings, old prisons and a hanging place, and a stone umbrella marking a victory of King Sahadeo. The walls run about 690 m from north to south.

chunar-fort.heading: Under the Company and the Raj
chunar-fort.body: Much of the fort as it stands today was built in Akbar's reign. From 1791 it was the headquarters of an invalid battalion of European and Indian troops, and from 1815 it held state prisoners. After it was formally ceded to the East India Company in 1818, it served for some years as the main artillery and ammunition depot of the North-Western Provinces. In 1849, after the British annexed the Sikh kingdom, Rani Jind Kaur was held here; she escaped in disguise and reached Kathmandu. Daniel Corrie, the chaplain who laid the foundation of St Mary's Church in Varanasi in 1810, also served at Chunar. Troops were withdrawn after 1890.

chunar-fort.heading: Chunar town: stone and pottery
chunar-fort.body: Chunar is a town in Mirzapur district on the Ganga. Its sandstone, Chunar Balua Patthar, received a Geographical Indication tag in 2019 and was used for the Lion Capital now in the Sarnath museum. The town is also known for Chunar Glaze Pottery, made of red clay: pieces are fired, brushed with a glaze of powdered glass and clay, and fired again. Workshops in the town let visitors watch artisans and try the craft. Durga Khoh, a temple with old inscriptions and figurines, and the Gangeshwar Nath temple are nearby. Chunar has been a filming location for the TV serial Chandrakanta and the series Mirzapur.

dev-deepawali.heading: Date and lamp-lighting time
dev-deepawali.body: Dev Deepawali is held on Kartik Purnima, the full moon of the month of Kartik, and the lamps are lit in pradosh kaal, the period just after sunset. For Varanasi, Drik Panchang puts the 2026 festival on Tuesday 24 November, with pradosh kaal from about 5:08 pm to 7:47 pm. The Purnima tithi lasts until 8:23 pm that day, so the calendar date and the date on the ghats are the same. The Uttar Pradesh holiday list for 2026 also gives 24 November for Kartik Purnima, together with Guru Nanak Jayanti. Morning bathing for Kartik Purnima happens the same day, so the ghats are busy from dawn.

dev-deepawali.heading: What happens on the ghats
dev-deepawali.body: At dusk, residents, ghat committees and volunteers light earthen lamps on the steps from the southern ghats to Rajghat, and on the far bank too. At Dashashwamedh Ghat the Ganga Seva Nidhi performs the Dev Deepawali maha aarti; in 2025 it ran from about 5:15 pm to 7:50 pm with 21 priests and 42 young women. Before it, a replica of the Amar Jawan Jyoti is lit and wreaths are laid for soldiers who died on duty. In recent years UP Tourism has also run a laser and projection show on the facade of Chet Singh Ghat, and a short green fireworks display on the sands opposite the Kashi Vishwanath Dham ghat. Check the 2026 programme closer to the date.

dev-deepawali.heading: Watching from a boat
dev-deepawali.body: From the river the whole lit riverfront is visible at once, and boats sell out weeks ahead. No official Dev Deepawali boat fare for 2026 had been announced when this was checked on 4 November. Press reports from October 2026 said the Alaknanda and Sam Manekshaw cruises were fully booked, and some event companies were selling seats at about ₹5,000 per person. UP Tourism (UPSTDC) has a four-day 'Dev Deepawali – Divya Kashi Anubhav' package with a special boat ride, reported from ₹15,999 per person on twin sharing. Every passenger must wear a life jacket, and a boat may not carry more people than its licence allows. After the 2026 floods, only large motorboats were cleared to run.

dev-deepawali.heading: Traffic, crowds and getting back
dev-deepawali.body: In 2025 the traffic police made the Godowlia–Maidagin stretch a no-vehicle zone, closed about a dozen routes to vehicles, and set up 22 parking areas, including Maidagin Town Hall and Beniabagh. E-rickshaws and autos ran on fixed routes. If a similar plan applies in 2026, a taxi can only reach the edge of the closed zone, and the last stretch to the ghats is on foot. Rooms near the ghats fill early; in 2024 late bookers were finding rooms 8–9 km out, near the highways. After the lamps the crowds leave together, so movement is slow until late at night. In an emergency, dial 112 for police; the Kashi Integrated Command and Control Centre helpline is 1533.

maha-shivratri.heading: Kashi Vishwanath on Shivratri night
maha-shivratri.body: On Maha Shivratri the temple's regular schedule gives way to four prahar aartis through the night. For 15 February 2026 the temple trust announced the Mangala aarti at 2:15–3:15 am and the prahar aartis at 10 pm–12:30 am, 1:30–2:30 am, 3:30–4:30 am and 5–6:15 am, with darshan continuing between them. The temple stayed open for 45 hours, and about 9.5 lakh devotees had darshan in that time. All online darshan and puja bookings for 15 and 16 February were cancelled, special darshan and aarti tickets were withdrawn, and sparsh darshan, touching the linga, was suspended.

maha-shivratri.heading: The Shiv Baraat
maha-shivratri.body: In the evening, processions celebrate the wedding of Shiva and Parvati. The largest, run by the Shiv Baraat Samiti, starts at the Mahamrityunjay Mahadev temple in Daranagar. Its traditional route passes Maidagin, Bulanala and Godowlia to Chitranjan Park, where the 'bride's side' welcomes the procession with thandai and garlands; in 2026 it went to Dedhsi Pul at Dashashwamedh. Other baraats leave from the Tilbhandeshwar Mahadev temple and the Lalkuti vyayamshala. Crowds line both sides of the road and fill rooftops and balconies. The Samiti held the baraat on Shivratri itself for 42 years in a row; in 2025 it moved to the next day because of Maha Kumbh crowds.

maha-shivratri.heading: Dhrupad Mela at Tulsi Ghat
maha-shivratri.body: In the days before Shivratri, Tulsi Ghat hosts the Dhrupad Mela, a five-day festival of dhrupad music that closes on Maha Shivratri, with the performances offered as tributes to Shiva. It was first held in 1975 and is organised by the Maharaj Banaras Vidya Mandir Nyas and the Dhrupad Samiti, with the Sankat Mochan mahant, Prof. Vishwambhar Nath Mishra, as coordinator. The 52nd edition opened on 11 February 2026 with more than 50 artists from India and abroad, including performers from the United States, Denmark, Russia and England. About 10 to 12 artists performed each day on the open ghat beside the river.

maha-shivratri.heading: Planning a Shivratri visit
maha-shivratri.body: Maha Shivratri falls on Phalguna Krishna Chaturdashi, the fourteenth day of the waning moon in Phalguna. It was on 15 February in 2026 and falls on Saturday 6 March 2027. In 2026 phones, digital watches, large bags, pens, plastic items, water bottles, tobacco, matches and lighters were not allowed into the Dham, so leave them at your hotel. Water, ORS and a medical desk were provided inside, and LED screens showed the rituals in the sanctum. Bring a warm layer for the pre-dawn queue, and do not pay anyone offering special darshan, aarti tickets or sparsh darshan, as all were cancelled.

ganga-mahotsav.heading: What is on stage
ganga-mahotsav.body: The festival is a series of evening concerts on an open-air stage by the river: Hindustani vocal and instrumental music, classical dance, folk song and devotional singing. In 2025 the bhajan singer Hansraj Raghuvanshi closed the festival, Padma Shri Malini Awasthi sang folk songs and Padma Shri Geeta Chandran danced Bharatanatyam, with Odissi, Kathak and sitar jugalbandis on other nights. In 2024, at Assi Ghat, Padma Bhushan Pandit Sajan Mishra sang on the opening night. For 2026 the divisional administration has asked for stage time for local talent, including winners of the Kashi Sansad cultural festival and students of the gurukul near Rajghat. No 2026 performer had been officially named by 4 November.

ganga-mahotsav.heading: Venues and the crafts fair
ganga-mahotsav.body: The festival has moved along the river over the years. In 2006 the opening Kathak was staged at Rajendra Prasad Ghat. Later editions were held at Rajghat; in 2024 the festival moved to Assi Ghat for the first time, and in 2025 it returned to Rajghat, with programmes at Namo Ghat as well. UP Tourism also holds a crafts fair as part of the festival at Urban Haat (Sanskritik Sankul), Chowka Ghat, away from the river. Its festival page lists a Ganga marathon and wrestling too, but the page was last updated in January 2022, so not every event is held every year. For 2026, stalls for ODOP (One District One Product) goods are planned at major ghats and hotels.

ganga-mahotsav.heading: Timings, entry and organisers
ganga-mahotsav.body: Ganga Mahotsav is a state festival run by the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department; the Varanasi divisional and district administration looks after the ghats, security, cleaning and traffic. The 2026 timings had not been announced by 4 November. In 2025 the programmes began at 4 pm each evening, and in 2024 they ran from 5 pm to 1 am. The concerts are held on open ghats, and no entry rules for 2026 have been published. The official line-up usually comes out only a few days ahead: in 2025 the artist list was released on 28–29 October, three days before the opening.

ganga-mahotsav.heading: Reaching Rajghat and Namo Ghat
ganga-mahotsav.body: Rajghat is at the northern end of the riverfront, beside the Malviya Bridge, near the point where the Varuna meets the Ganga. The small Kashi railway station stands on the high bank above the ghat; the main station is Varanasi Junction (Cantt). Namo Ghat is a short walk north along the river, and its broad, step-free promenade is easier for older visitors, wheelchairs and prams than the steep steps of the southern ghats. No traffic plan for the 2026 festival nights had been published by 4 November. The last evening runs straight into Dev Deepawali on 24 November, which has its own road closures.

bharat-milap.heading: How the lila unfolds
bharat-milap.body: The Bharat Milap is staged by the Shri Chitrakoot Ramlila Samiti as part of its Ramlila, which tradition traces to the devotee Megha Bhagat. On the day, Yadav devotees in white dhotis and turbans carry the Pushpak Vimaan, reported to weigh about five tonnes, with Ram, Lakshman and Sita from the Chitrakoot ground to Nati Imli, which stands for Ayodhya. Bharat and Shatrughan arrive with the people of Ayodhya and wait on the eastern side of the ground. When Ram and Lakshman step down, they run 84 steps to embrace their brothers, who lie prostrate before them. The meeting lasts only about five minutes and ends with flower showers and chants.

bharat-milap.heading: Timing, the royal family and the crowd
bharat-milap.body: The meeting takes place at twilight, at about 4:40 pm. In 2026 Ram's party reached the ground at about 4:10 pm, Kunwar Anant Narayan Singh of the Kashi royal family arrived on three elephants with his two sons at about 4:25 pm, and Bharat and Shatrughan came at 4:35 pm. Amar Ujala put the 2026 crowd at more than three lakh. The event is counted among Kashi's 'lakkha melas', fairs that draw lakhs, and many people wait three to four hours for a few minutes of darshan. Akashvani Varanasi broadcast the 2026 lila live on 1242 kHz medium wave and Vividh Bharati FM 100.6 MHz.

bharat-milap.heading: How the date is fixed
bharat-milap.body: The organisers hold the lila on Papankusha Ekadashi, the eleventh day of the bright half of Ashwin. In most years this is the day after Vijayadashami. In 2026 the Kashi panchangs placed Ekadashi two days after Dussehra, so the lila was held on Thursday 22 October; the Samiti's manager said it was the first time the lila had not fallen on the day after Vijayadashami. Schools in Varanasi were closed that day. When planning, go by the Ekadashi date announced locally rather than counting one day from Dussehra.

nag-nathaiya.heading: The lila on Tulsi Ghat
nag-nathaiya.body: Nag Nathaiya is organised at Tulsi Ghat by the Akhara Goswami Tulsidas, under the guidance of the Sankat Mochan temple's mahant, Prof. Vishwambhar Nath Mishra. On the morning of the lila a kadamba branch is brought from the grove in the Sankat Mochan temple grounds and fixed on the bank. In the afternoon the boy playing Krishna plays ball with his friends until the ball falls into the river, which stands for the Yamuna. He climbs the branch and leaps in, while boatmen-divers wait in the water. He rises on the hoods of a seven-hooded Kaliya about 22 feet long, receives aarti, and rides the serpent along the river so the crowd can see him.

nag-nathaiya.heading: Where to watch
nag-nathaiya.body: Spectators fill the steps of Tulsi Ghat and the ghats around it, from Assi up to Chet Singh Ghat, and boats and bajras crowd the river in front. Amar Ujala put the 2024 crowd at about 1.5 lakh, and the event is counted among Kashi's 'lakkha melas', fairs that draw lakhs. By tradition the Kashi royal family watches from a bajra; in 2024 Kunwar Anant Narayan Singh came by boat with his family. While the lila is on, boat traffic in front of Tulsi Ghat is stopped. When the river is high, police, PAC and NDRF teams are posted on the ghats, as in 2022.

nag-nathaiya.heading: Date and time
nag-nathaiya.body: The lila falls on Kartik Shukla Chaturthi, the fourth day of the bright half of Kartik, four days after Diwali. It takes place in the late afternoon, as the sun begins to go down: in 2023 Krishna's procession came down the steps at about 4 pm, and in 2022 the leap came at about 4:40 pm. The main episode lasts only about 10 to 15 minutes. In 2026 the Chaturthi falls on Friday 13 November, the same day as Nahay Khay, the first day of Chhath, and in 2027 on Tuesday 2 November. Crowds start gathering from early afternoon.

buddha-purnima.heading: Relic darshan at Mulagandha Kuti Vihar
buddha-purnima.body: The central event at Sarnath is darshan of the Buddha's sacred relics at Mulagandha Kuti Vihar. They are shown to the public only twice a year: on Buddha Purnima, and during a three-day observance ending on Kartik Purnima in November. On Buddha Purnima 2026 darshan ran from 6 am to 11 am. Amar Ujala reported about two lakh devotees in those five hours, with a queue about a kilometre long from the main Sarnath crossing to the temple. Heads of the Thai, Cambodian, Chinese, Tibetan, Myanmar and Bhutanese temples in Sarnath took part in installing the relics, and devotees also walk around the Dhamek Stupa.

buddha-purnima.heading: The day's programme in 2026
buddha-purnima.body: Monks led a special puja for world peace in the morning. A Dhamma assembly with cultural programmes ran from noon to 3 pm, and at 4 pm a Dhamma Yatra set out from the Dr Ambedkar memorial park at Kachahri, passing Golghar, Pandeypur and Pahadiya to reach Sarnath. A Dhamma desana, a sermon, followed at 6 pm. A medical camp ran from 10 am to 5 pm, and food dana was served from morning to 10 pm at the Maha Bodhi Society of India premises. The temple complex was lit with more than 5,000 lamps, and pilgrims came from countries including Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos, Korea and Bhutan.

buddha-purnima.heading: Date and getting there
buddha-purnima.body: Buddha Purnima is the full moon of Vaishakha, which falls in April or May. In 2026 it fell on Friday 1 May, and in 2027 it falls on Thursday 20 May. Pilgrims start arriving a day or two before; in 2026 most had reached Sarnath by the previous evening. Sarnath is about 10 km north-east of central Varanasi. The relics are shown only in the morning, and the afternoon Dhamma Yatra follows the main road from Kachahri through Pandeypur, so plan to travel early. The Sarnath Archaeological Museum is closed on Fridays.

ramnagar-ramlila.heading: An evening at the Ramlila
ramnagar-ramlila.body: Each evening stages one or more episodes of Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas. Ramayanis chant the verses, and the swaroops, the boys who play Ram, Sita, Lakshman, Bharat and Shatrughan, then speak their lines. Lead roles go to boys under 14, mostly from Brahmin families, who train for about two months beforehand. Devotees carry the swaroops on their shoulders to the site. The Kashi royal family attends every day, arriving on elephants. Light comes from petromax lamps, torches and lanterns, and the actors project their voices without microphones. Thousands watch, yet the crowd stays quiet enough to hear them.

ramnagar-ramlila.heading: The sites and the nemis
ramnagar-ramlila.body: The lila uses about 20 fixed sites spread over some 5 km of Ramnagar, including Ayodhya, Janakpur, Chitrakoot, Panchavati, Nishadraj's ashram, Ashok Vatika, Lanka and Rambagh. On the opening evening, at dusk, the pond at Rambagh becomes the Kshir Sagar, the ocean of milk, with a tableau of Vishnu. Sites can be more than a kilometre apart, and the audience walks with the actors from one to the next. The most devoted spectators, called nemis, come every evening for the whole month, many with a copy of the Manas in hand, following the text as the lila moves.

ramnagar-ramlila.heading: Dates and daily timing
ramnagar-ramlila.body: The Ramlila opens on Anant Chaturdashi with the birth of Ravan and runs for 31 days to Ashwin (Sharad) Purnima, so Dussehra falls within it. In 2026 it began on Friday 25 September. The lila usually starts at about 5 pm and runs to about 9 pm, though some evenings go on later into the night. The last episode is a discourse on Ram's teachings after his coronation. The cast is usually announced in early August, after the first Ganesh puja at Chowk. The 2027 schedule had not been published by November 2026; the calendar points to mid-September to mid-October.

ramnagar-ramlila.heading: Getting there and what to expect
ramnagar-ramlila.body: Ramnagar is on the east bank of the Ganga, opposite Tulsi Ghat, about 14 km from Varanasi by road. There is no ticket counter and no fixed seating: the audience stands or sits on the ground and moves with the actors. Arrive before 5 pm to see the royal procession and find a place. The lila is treated as a religious ritual rather than a show; many spectators come freshly bathed, with tilak and sandalwood paste, and the crowd keeps silent during the dialogue. Plan your return in advance, as the evening ends after dark on the far bank.

shravan.heading: Dates and Sawan Mondays
shravan.body: Uttar Pradesh follows the purnimanta calendar, in which the month of Shravan ends on Shravan Purnima (Raksha Bandhan). In 2026 the month ran from 30 July to 28 August, with Sawan Mondays on 3, 10, 17 and 24 August. In 2027 it runs from 19 July to 17 August, with five Mondays: 19 and 26 July and 2, 9 and 16 August. Mondays, sacred to Shiva, bring the largest crowds. For the first Monday of 2026 the temple administration expected about four lakh devotees between the Mangala and Shayan aartis, against about 3.41 lakh on the first Monday of 2025, and it prepared for about 80 lakh over the month.

shravan.heading: Darshan arrangements on Mondays
shravan.body: On Sawan Mondays the administration cancels sparsh darshan, touching the linga, and all daily passes, and devotees have darshan from outside the sanctum. In 2026 Sugam Darshan was also withheld on 10, 17 and 24 August. Queues form behind barricades in seven lines that start from Maidagin, Dashashwamedh Ghat, Godowlia, Jangambari, Vishwanath Gali and Bansphatak and lead to seven gates; devotees who bathe at the ghats enter through the Ganga Dwar. Free golf carts on the Godowlia–Maidagin road carry elderly and differently-abled devotees, and screens at seven points in the Dham show live darshan.

shravan.heading: Kanwariyas and road closures
shravan.body: Kanwariyas carrying Ganga water arrive at the Dham throughout the month. In 2026 the left lane of the Prayagraj road, from the Gudiya border at Mirzamurad through Rajatalab and Mohansarai to Chandpur, was reserved for kanwar traffic for all of Shravan. Around the Sawan Mondays the route to the Dham was kept for kanwariyas from Saturday 8 pm to Tuesday 8 am, and heavy and inter-district vehicles were barred from the city. Maidagin–Chowk–Godowlia is a no-vehicle zone every day, and the approaches to the Dham and Dashashwamedh Ghat are for pedestrians only.

shravan.heading: Monsoon on the river
shravan.body: Shravan falls in the monsoon, when the Ganga rises. On 17 August 2026 all 84 ghats and their steps were under water, and the Ganga Seva Nidhi moved the Dashashwamedh aarti to the roof of its office. On 22 August the district administration halted all boat services, and cremations at Manikarnika moved to higher ground. In a high-water year, expect flooded ghats and possible boat bans. Many devotees also visit other Shiva temples in Sawan, such as Tilbhandeshwar in Bengali Tola and Markandeya Mahadev at Kaithi, about 30 km from the city.

ganga-dussehra.heading: Bathing and offerings
ganga-dussehra.body: The day begins with snan and daan: a dip in the Ganga, followed by acts of charity. In 2026 Amar Ujala reported about three lakh people bathing between 4 am and 9 am, at ghats including Dashashwamedh, Assi, Rajendra Prasad, Sheetla, Panchganga and Manikarnika. Many then went on to the Annapurna and Kashi Vishwanath temples for darshan. Through the day, groups make offerings to the river: milk abhishek, saris and chunari, and food. In 2026, 56 families offered 56 dishes at Assi Ghat, and thousands of saris sent from several states and from the United States were offered.

ganga-dussehra.heading: Aartis and evening programmes
ganga-dussehra.body: Rituals run on the ghats from morning to night. The Shri Kashi Vishwanath temple trust holds a morning aarti at Lalita Ghat and rituals in the Dham. At Dashashwamedh Ghat the Ganga Seva Nidhi holds its Ganga Dussehra festival from about 6 pm, with Vedic puja by 11 priests and a maha aarti in which 22 young women appear as Riddhi and Siddhi; in 2026 the ghat was lit with about 11,000 lamps and decorated with 25 quintals of flowers. Other groups hold worship at Panchganga, Ahilyabai and Namo ghats, and near the Sheetla temple the Gangotri Seva Samiti performs a 501-litre milk abhishek.

ganga-dussehra.heading: How the date is set
ganga-dussehra.body: Ganga Dussehra falls on Jyeshtha Shukla Dashami, the tenth day of the bright half of Jyeshtha, in May or June. Varanasi follows the local panchang and the udaya tithi, the tithi current at sunrise, so the city's date can differ by a day from some printed calendars. In 2026 the main bathing day in Varanasi was Tuesday 26 May, while Drik Panchang and Aaj Tak listed 25 May. In 2027 it falls on Sunday 13 June. The festival comes in the summer heat: in 2026 it fell on the second day of Nautapa.

ganga-dussehra.heading: Crowds, heat and safety
ganga-dussehra.body: In 2026 the main bathing took place between 4 am and 9 am, before the worst of the Nautapa heat. For that year's festival the police deployed more than 2,200 personnel, four PAC companies and an RAF company, with three water police teams, four NDRF teams and three drone teams on and along the river. The evening programme at Dashashwamedh draws large crowds, so arrive well before 6 pm for a place on the steps. Bathe only at the main ghats where police and rescue teams are posted, and stay in shallow water.

rangbhari-masaan-holi.heading: Rangbhari Ekadashi at Kashi Vishwanath
rangbhari-masaan-holi.body: In Kashi, Holi begins on Rangbhari Ekadashi. The temple's chief executive officer describes the day as Gauri's gauna: after their wedding on Mahashivratri, Shiva brings Parvati home to the Dham. Devotees put gulal on Baba Vishwanath's forehead and offer abir at Parvati's feet, asking leave to start playing Holi. By custom, the gauna rites begin at the former mahant's house at Tedhi Neem, where the palki is worshipped, and the movable (chal) images of Vishwanath, Parvati and Ganesh are taken out in a palki procession. In 2026 the Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan of Mathura sent gulal, fruit and dry fruits as offerings to the jyotirlinga.

rangbhari-masaan-holi.heading: The day inside the Dham
rangbhari-masaan-holi.body: In 2026 the midday bhog aarti drew a large crowd. In the evening the chal image of the Shiva family was placed in the sanctum, followed by the Saptarishi aarti. Children from Braj performed raas and played Holi with flowers on the Shivarchan Manch in the temple complex, and the cultural programme ran until about 10 pm. Thandai and light refreshments were arranged for devotees. The temple's chief executive officer said the arrangements had been strengthened that year, and that gifts and cultural exchanges took place between the Kashi Vishwanath Dham and the Shri Krishna Janmasthan in Mathura.

rangbhari-masaan-holi.heading: Masaan Holi at the cremation ghats
rangbhari-masaan-holi.body: The next day, Holi is played with ash from the pyres (chita bhasma) at Manikarnika and Harishchandra, Kashi's two cremation ghats. In 2025 it followed an aarti of Baba Mahashmashan Nath and lasted about an hour from noon; Naga sadhus and devotees smeared ash and gulal while cremations went on. Preparations start about six months ahead, with ash gathered daily from the cremation ground. The custom is disputed: the Kashi Vidvat Parishad, a council of Sanskrit scholars, calls it unscriptural and recent, while the organisers say playing Holi with funeral ash is mentioned in religious texts.

rangbhari-masaan-holi.heading: Restrictions in recent years
rangbhari-masaan-holi.body: In 2025 the Baba Mahashmashan Nath temple committee asked women not to attend, citing the size of the crowd. In 2026 the Varanasi police placed curbs on the ash Holi at Manikarnika, and Hindustan Times reported that devotees played on the ghat despite them. Permission and its conditions are decided each year by the police, on grounds of law and order and crowd control, so check the current rules before you go.

chhath.heading: Four days, step by step
chhath.body: Chhath opens with Nahay Khay. On the second day, Kharna, women cook kheer with jaggery and wheat roti called sohari in clay, brass or bronze vessels, offer it to Surya and Chhathi Maiya, and then eat it. A 36-hour nirjala fast, without even water, begins after Kharna. On the third day the vratis offer sandhya arghya to the setting sun from the river, and on the fourth morning usha arghya to the rising sun, which ends the festival. Thekua, a sweet prasad, is made at home for the offerings.

chhath.heading: What is offered, and where
chhath.body: Arghya is given with milk and water while devotees repeat the mantra 'Om Ghrini Suryaya Namah'. The soop holds thekua, fruit, coconut, sugarcane and rice laddoos; Amar Ujala counted about 30 kinds of fruit, five vegetables, five grains and some 40 puja items among what women prepare. Besides the city ghats, arghya is offered at kunds, ponds and sarovars, at riverside ghats around Chaubepur such as Markandey Mahadev Ghat, and at Tilmapur near Sarnath. In 2025 women were building their puja vedis on Assi Ghat two days before the festival began.

chhath.heading: Arrangements on the river
chhath.body: Before the festival, Nagar Nigam teams clear mud from ghats such as Reewa, Ganga Mahal and Tulsi and clean the ghats. In 2025 bamboo barricades went up at the ghats, and water barricades in the Ganga kept people out of deep water. NDRF, water police, PAC and divers were posted at the ghats, drones and CCTV watched the crowds, plain-clothes women police were on duty, and public-address systems were set up. The police commissioner inspected the ghats from Namo Ghat to Assi and Ravidas Ghat, and traffic diversions, no-entry points and temporary parking were set on the routes to the ghats.

chhath.heading: Dates and arghya times
chhath.body: Chhath runs from Kartik Shukla Chaturthi to Saptami, so its dates move each year. In 2026 Nahay Khay is on 13 November, Kharna on 14 November, the evening arghya on 15 November and the dawn arghya on 16 November. Drik Panchang gives sunset in Varanasi at about 5:10 pm on 15 November and sunrise at about 6:15 am. In 2027 the four days fall from 2 to 5 November. In 2025 the Kashi panchang gave a window of only 48 minutes for the evening arghya and 57 minutes for the morning one, and crowds began gathering at the ghats from the afternoon.

ravidas-jayanti.heading: A two-week mela at Seer Govardhanpur
ravidas-jayanti.body: The celebration at the birthplace temple near Banaras Hindu University runs for about 15 days, with the main events on two days. Devotees arrive from Punjab, Haryana, other states and abroad; about 1,000 NRIs were expected in 2026. The head of Dera Sachkhand Ballan in Jalandhar travels to Kashi by special train with the sangat. In 2025 about 3,000 devotees boarded the Begumpura Express with him at Jalandhar after a procession through the city, and Amar Ujala reported that about 3 lakh followers of Guru Ravidas had reached Kashi for that year's Jayanti.

ravidas-jayanti.heading: Langar, tents and sewa
ravidas-jayanti.body: Langar runs through the mela. In 2026 more than half a dozen langars operated, two run by the temple trust and the rest by devotees from Punjab, supplied by more than 100 trucks of provisions. In the days before the Jayanti about 5 lakh people a day were being fed, and the number was expected to reach 15 to 20 lakh a day at the peak. More than 150 tents were put up for pilgrims to stay in, and about 5,000 volunteers handled the services.

ravidas-jayanti.heading: The Janam Asthan temple
ravidas-jayanti.body: The foundation stone was laid on 14 June 1965 by Sant Hari Dass, under the guidance of Sant Sarwan Dass, and volunteers built the temple. The image of Guru Ravidas was installed in 1974. Built in a gurdwara style, the temple has a large dome and 31 smaller gold-plated domes, and holds more than 200 kg of donated gold, including a gold palki of about 130 kg. The commemorative Guru Ravidas Gate was inaugurated in 1998 by President K. R. Narayanan.

ravidas-jayanti.heading: When it falls
ravidas-jayanti.body: Guru Ravidas Jayanti is kept on Magh Purnima, the full moon of the month of Magh, so the date moves between late January and February. In 2026 it fell on Sunday 1 February, the 649th birth anniversary, and the special train from Jalandhar was due in Kashi on the Friday before. In 2027 Drik Panchang puts the Jayanti on Saturday 20 February, the 650th birth anniversary. The two main days around the full moon are the busiest; through the rest of the year the temple is open for darshan, with langar.

kabir-jayanti.heading: Prakatya Utsav at Lahartara
kabir-jayanti.body: Kabir Panthis call the day Kabir's prakatya, his appearance, recalling the legend that he was found as a baby on a lotus in Lahartara pond, and that Neeru and Neema took him home and raised him. Sadguru Kabir Prakatya Dham manages about 8 acres of the old 17-acre pond. In 2026 its three-day festival opened on 27 June with the hoisting of the Satyanam flag, worship and aarti, followed by bhajan, sakhi and satsang, a bhandara on each day, and a national seminar, 'Kabir ki Virasat: Kashi se Maghar tak', on 28 and 29 June.

kabir-jayanti.heading: Kabirchaura Math, the Mool Gadi
kabir-jayanti.body: Kabirchaura Math, the Mool Gadi of the Kabir Panth, was founded by Surat Gopal, described as a direct disciple of Kabir. The complex holds the Beejak Mandir, built on the old platform for discourse; the platforms where Kabir talked with his followers; his wooden sandals in the Smriti Kaksh; a samadhi and a mazaar dedicated to him; and Neeru Teela, the resting place of Neeru and Nima. On the Jayanti the math holds bhajan satsang, a music evening and rituals, alongside programmes at other Kabir maths in the city. It is open from about 5 am to 8 pm.

kabir-jayanti.heading: The Kabirdham Yatra and Nirgun music
kabir-jayanti.body: In 2026 Kabir Prakatya Dham led a Kabirdham Yatra of about 225 km from Maghar, where Kabir died, to Kashi, his birthplace. More than 200 sadhus and followers from Nepal and eight Indian states took part, halting at Kabir maths and ashrams for satsang and bhajan-kirtan; a Kashi-to-Maghar yatra had been held in 2017. Sant Kabir Academy, Maghar, also organised the Nirgun Tridhara Bhakti Utsav across Maghar, Ghazipur and Varanasi from 27 to 29 June 2026, with Nirgun bhakti singers, scholars and folk artists.

kabir-jayanti.heading: When it falls
kabir-jayanti.body: Kabir Jayanti is kept on Jyeshtha Purnima, the full moon of Jyeshtha. When the lunar year adds an extra month (adhik maas) to Jyeshtha, as it did in 2026, Lahartara's main celebration moves about a month later, to the full moon of the regular (nija) Jyeshtha: 29 June in 2026. That year some maths, such as one in Pali district of Rajasthan, planned to keep the earlier full moon instead. In 2027 Drik Panchang puts the Jayanti on Friday 18 June.

guru-nanak-jayanti.heading: The day at the gurdwaras
guru-nanak-jayanti.body: At Gurdwara Guru Ka Bagh the Gurpurab begins before dawn with Asa Di Vaar, followed by kirtan and a langar that runs through the day. Ragi jathas from Guru Ka Bagh and Nichibagh sing shabad kirtan, the granthis give katha in the evening, and the sangat keeps arriving from early morning until late at night. An Akhand Path, the unbroken reading of all 1,430 pages of the Guru Granth Sahib by a relay of readers, takes about 48 hours and ends with the bhog ceremony.

guru-nanak-jayanti.heading: Guru Ka Bagh and Guru Nanak's visit
guru-nanak-jayanti.body: Guru Nanak reached Kashi at Shivaratri in 1507 (1563 Bikrami) and rested in a shady garden. There Pandit Chatur Das asked why he wore no sectarian marks; the Guru answered that only the Name of God counts, and that the truly learned remember God and serve others. The garden no longer exists. The present gurdwara on Guru Nanak Road was inaugurated on 23 November 1969 for the Guru's 500th birth anniversary. It has a divan hall, a library and rooms for staff and pilgrims, and Guru Nanak Khalsa Balika Inter College stands beside it.

guru-nanak-jayanti.heading: Other gurdwaras to visit
guru-nanak-jayanti.body: Gurdwara Bari Sangat at Nichibagh stands on the site of the house where Guru Tegh Bahadur stayed for several months in 1666. It keeps the room where he meditated as his Tap Asthan, a narrow well called Baoli Ganga Pargat, two of his cholas and the soles of his shoes, a pair of Guru Gobind Singh's shoes, and 17 hukamnamas addressed to the sangat. Guru Gobind Singh came here as a child in 1670. Gurdwara Chhoti Sangat, visited by both Gurus, keeps a handwritten Guru Granth Sahib copied in February 1777.

guru-nanak-jayanti.heading: Date, and Dev Deepawali on the same day
guru-nanak-jayanti.body: The Gurpurab is kept on Kartik Purnima, so its date moves each year. In 2026 it falls on Tuesday 24 November, the date in the SGPC's Nanakshahi calendar, and the same day as Dev Deepawali on the ghats. In 2027 the two fall on different days: Dev Deepawali on 13 November and the Gurpurab on 14 November. On Dev Deepawali 2025 traffic police made the Godowlia–Maidagin stretch a no-vehicle zone and closed about a dozen routes to vehicles, so allow extra time for travel across the city on the evening of 24 November.

parshvanath-janma-kalyanak.heading: Three days of fasting and worship
parshvanath-janma-kalyanak.body: At Bhelupur the birth of Parshvanath is marked over three days. In 2021 the Shri Jain Shwetambar Tirth Society organised the celebration: men and women kept a strict fast on Navami, Dashami and Ekadashi, taking only water, and on the second day a procession went from the Jain temple at Bhadaini to the temple at Bhelupur. The Posh Dashami vrat described in Jain sources spans the same three tithis, with ekasana (one meal a day) on each day, worship of Parshvanath, and japa of his mantra on a mala.

parshvanath-janma-kalyanak.heading: The temples at Bhelupur
parshvanath-janma-kalyanak.body: The Bhelupur tirtha belongs to both the Digambar and Shvetambar traditions. It has three temples, a Digambar temple, a Shvetambar temple and a Parshvanath–Padmavati temple, and keeps footprints associated with Parshvanath. The Digambar temple worships a black-stone image of Parshvanath of about 75 cm, dated to the 9th–11th centuries CE; the Shvetambar temple has a white image of about 60 cm. Jain tradition names King Ashvasena and Queen Vama as his parents, and the 14th-century Vividha Tirtha Kalpa of Jinaprabha Suri describes the temple.

parshvanath-janma-kalyanak.heading: Four Tirthankaras of Kashi
parshvanath-janma-kalyanak.body: Jains hold Varanasi as the birthplace of four Tirthankaras. Besides Parshvanath at Bhelupur, Suparshvanatha is linked with Bhadaini, Chandraprabha with Chandrawati, and Shreyansanatha with the Sarnath–Singhpuri area. Bhelupur is also held as the place of Parshvanath's conception and renunciation. Jain tradition places his kevala jnana at Ahichchhatra and his nirvana at Sammed Shikhar, Parasnath Hill in present-day Jharkhand. Mahavira is also said to have preached in Varanasi and Sarnath.

parshvanath-janma-kalyanak.heading: When it falls
parshvanath-janma-kalyanak.body: The date follows the lunar calendar. In the purnimanta reckoning of north India it is Paush Krishna Dashami; in the amanta calendar of Gujarat the same day is Magshar Vad 10. Some sources give the next day, Paush Krishna Ekadashi, as the birth date. Because of how the months fall, there is no Posh Dashami in calendar year 2026: the last one was in mid-December 2025, and the next ones are on 2 January 2027 and 22 December 2027. Temple panchangs can differ by a day, so confirm with the Bhelupur temples.

christmas.heading: Midnight Mass and the crib
christmas.body: Christmas begins at midnight on 24 December. In 2022 carols rang out at midnight in all 44 churches of Varanasi, large and small, and the bishop of the Varanasi diocese led the rites. After the midnight Mass a statue of the infant Jesus is carried in procession from the church to the crib, where worshippers bow before it. Churches and homes put up cribs and Christmas trees, cake is shared, and church programmes with tableaux and carols run for about a week after Christmas, into early January.

christmas.heading: St Mary's Cathedral and its fair
christmas.body: St Mary's Cathedral in the Cantonment, completed in 1992, borrows from Hindu temple architecture: a tiered, mountain-like form, porches like mandapas, a sixteen-sided base and jalis that tell the story of Christ, under a 30-metre steel cross. Its nativity scene draws many visitors at Christmas. Outside, a fair with food stalls, swings and rides runs from Christmas Day. In 2021 the cathedral also held a three-day exhibition of tableaux of Christ's birth and miracles, which drew more than 10,000 people a day, and mission-school students staged a dance drama.

christmas.heading: Other churches and Bhojpuri carols
christmas.body: St Mary's Church, also in the Cantonment, is the city's first Protestant church: its foundation was laid on 29 April 1810, and it was finished in 1812 for the British garrison. Each Christmas it is lit with fairy lights and carols are sung. Christmas reports also name Lal Church, St Paul's Church at Sigra, St Thomas Church at Godowlia, and churches at Ramkatora and Teliyabagh; Lal Church holds a bonfire service. At the Mahmoorganj church, known as the Bhojpuri church, services and carols have been in Bhojpuri since 1986.

christmas.heading: Planning for Christmas week
christmas.body: Christmas Day is fixed: Friday 25 December in 2026 and Saturday 25 December in 2027. The Christmas–New Year week is the busiest of the winter at Kashi Vishwanath: in 2025 the temple suspended VIP, protocol and sparsh darshan from 24 December.
