Fog is common from mid-December and delays morning flights and trains. Nights are cold, with an average December low of about 10 °C at the Babatpur weather station, so dress warmly for midnight Mass.

kashi-tamil-sangamam-festival.heading: What delegates do in Kashi
kashi-tamil-sangamam-festival.body: Each delegation travels for eight days, four of them spent on visits and programmes in Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya. In Varanasi, groups in earlier editions visited Kashi Vishwanath, Kedar Ghat, Sarnath, the ancestral home of the poet Subramania Bharati and the city's Tamil heritage pockets, and met Tamil-speaking families. Seminars, lecture-demonstrations and cultural programmes bring them together with people from Kashi, and exhibitions sell handlooms, handicrafts, One District One Product goods, books and regional food.

kashi-tamil-sangamam-festival.heading: Past editions
kashi-tamil-sangamam-festival.body: The first edition ran from 16 November to 15 December 2022, with more than 2,500 participants and daily cultural programmes at BHU. The second, from 17 to 30 December 2023, was held at Namo Ghat; its exhibition drew more than 2 lakh visitors and recorded ₹22 lakh in sales. The third, from 15 to 24 February 2025, focused on the sage Agastya and took delegates to the Maha Kumbh at Prayagraj. The fourth was inaugurated at Namo Ghat on 2 December 2025 on the theme 'Tamil Karkalam' (Let us learn Tamil) and closed at Rameswaram on 15 December.

kashi-tamil-sangamam-festival.heading: Learning Tamil in Varanasi
kashi-tamil-sangamam-festival.body: Recent editions also reach beyond the delegations. In December 2025, 50 Hindi-knowing Tamil teachers trained at the Central Institute of Classical Tamil taught short spoken-Tamil modules in 50 Varanasi schools, reaching about 1,500 students, and 300 college students from Uttar Pradesh went to Tamil Nadu in ten batches to study Tamil. For 2026, Thirukkural experts from Tamil Nadu are to visit schools and colleges in Varanasi, and the National Book Trust is to hold reading and storytelling sessions in Varanasi schools.

kashi-tamil-sangamam-festival.heading: If you are in Varanasi during the Sangamam
kashi-tamil-sangamam-festival.body: Delegates must be from Tamil Nadu and register on the official portal, kashitamil.iitm.ac.in; registration for 2026 closes on 13 November. As of 2 November 2026 the venues and times of the inauguration on 28 November and the closing programme on 12 December had not been announced, and the organisers had not said whether the public can attend. Visitors can still see Tamil Kashi on their own: Hanuman Ghat, once called Rameswaram Ghat, Subramania Bharati's family home there, the South Indian maths in the lanes behind it, and Kedar Ghat a short walk south.

lolark-shashthi.heading: The night bath and the vow
lolark-shashthi.body: Bathing begins after midnight. In 2026 a Rudrabhishek and shodashopachar puja of Lolarkeshwar Mahadev, whose temple stands beside the kund, was held at 11 pm the night before. Astrologers gave the best window for bathing and worship as 6:31 to 10:26 am on 17 September, with bathing, charity and darshan continuing until sunset. Couples bathe together and, by local belief, leave behind the clothes they bathed in. Couples whose prayer has been answered come back to fulfil their vow (mannat).

lolark-shashthi.heading: The kund and its story
lolark-shashthi.body: Lolark Kund is a sun kund. By belief, a wheel of the Sun's chariot fell here and the pit filled with water. The tank is about 50 feet deep, with steps on three sides leading down to an inverted-pyramid basin, and Ganga water still enters through an underground source in the rains. Local tradition tells of a king of Cooch Behar, cured of a skin disease and blessed with a son after bathing here, who had the steps made of gold. Renovations are also credited to Ahilyabai Holkar. The Kashi Khanda (chapter 46) praises bathing and prayer here.

lolark-shashthi.heading: Crowds and arrangements in 2026
lolark-shashthi.body: Couples came from about ten states, among them Bihar, Jharkhand, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. They began arriving on 15 September, and by that night a queue more than 1 km long stood behind barricades from Sonarpura towards the Assi road. By the morning of 17 September more than one lakh couples had bathed. The line ran about 3 km along the main road, with barricades from Bhadaini to Shivala, and police watched the crowd with drones and plain-clothes officers.

lolark-shashthi.heading: When it falls
lolark-shashthi.body: Lolark Shashthi is Bhadrapada Shukla Shashthi, kept on the day when Shashthi prevails at sunrise (the udaya tithi). In 2026 Shashthi ran by the local panchang from 8:55 am on 16 September to 10:26 am on the 17th, so the bath fell on 17 September. In 2027 Drik Panchang shows Shashthi at sunrise on Monday 6 September; the tithi begins at 11:17 am on 5 September, so expect queues to form from the night of the 5th.

kashi-vishwanath-corridor.heading: How much the temple precinct grew
kashi-vishwanath-corridor.body: Before the project, the temple premises covered only about 3,000 square feet and were reached through narrow, crowded lanes. At the opening, the Prime Minister said the temple and its premises could now take 50,000 to 75,000 devotees. Building the Dham meant buying more than 300 properties around the temple through negotiation, and about 1,400 shopkeepers, tenants and homeowners were rehabilitated. In December 2021 the government said that no case over these acquisitions or the rehabilitation was pending in any court.

kashi-vishwanath-corridor.heading: Buildings, access and rediscovered temples
kashi-vishwanath-corridor.body: The government's list of the 23 phase 1 buildings also includes a Tourist Facilitation Centre, a Mumukshu Bhavan and a Bhogshala, alongside the Yatri Suvidha Kendras (pilgrim facility centres). The project was designed with ramps, escalators and other facilities for elderly and disabled visitors. While old buildings were being cleared, more than 40 ancient temples were found. The government says they were restored and beautified without any change to their original structure.

kashi-vishwanath-corridor.heading: Arriving from the river
kashi-vishwanath-corridor.body: The corridor's river entrance is Ganga Dwar at Lalita Ghat, so a visit can begin with a boat ride or a walk along the ghats, and then lead straight up to the temple. Under the municipal rate list fixed in June 2023, a boat from Ganga Dwar to Assi Ghat or to Namo Ghat and back costs ₹175 per person. The corporation said boards with these rates would be put up at the ghats, so check the board and agree the fare before boarding.

kashi-vishwanath-corridor.heading: Timings, gates and what to leave behind
kashi-vishwanath-corridor.body: The temple trust lists the temple as open from 2:30 am to 11 pm. General darshan runs from 4 am to 11 am, from noon to 7 pm, and again from about 8:30 pm to 9 pm, between the aartis. The administration's guidelines bar mobile phones and smartwatches inside; free lockers are available at the Yatri Suvidha Kendras. For Sawan 2026 the Dham used seven separate entry and exit gates. Sugam Darshan, the trust's paid queue-less darshan, costs ₹300 per person on its official portal.

namo-ghat.heading: The Namaste sculptures and what is on the ghat
namo-ghat.body: The ghat is known for its 'Namaste' sculptures of folded hands, which face the rising sun over the Ganga. The first phase installed two, about 25 feet and 15 feet tall, and the divisional commissioner said in November 2024 that a 75-foot metal sculpture was added in the second phase. Officials also list a library, a lounge, bathing pools, changing rooms, a yoga area, a children's play area, a café and a food court serving Banarasi dishes.

namo-ghat.heading: Boats, CNG and the hydrogen ferry
namo-ghat.body: Namo Ghat has the country's first floating CNG station for boats, and a separate CNG station for road vehicles. From its jetty, boats go to the Ganga Aarti and to the Kashi Vishwanath Dham. The municipal fare for a round trip between Assi Ghat and Namo Ghat is ₹345 per person, a rate set in June 2023 and fixed again in January 2025. In December 2025 India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell passenger vessel, a 50-seat air-conditioned catamaran, began commercial service from Namo Ghat.

namo-ghat.heading: Location and access
namo-ghat.body: Namo Ghat is at the northern end of the riverfront, between Raj Ghat and Adikeshav Ghat, next to the Rajghat bridge. The redeveloped 'model ghat' stretch runs about 1.5 km towards Adikeshav Ghat. Unlike most ghats, it can be reached by car: vehicles drive up to the entrance, and parking is available. A ramp gives elderly and disabled visitors easy access to the river. Kashi railway station is the closest; from the city's main stations, an auto takes about 15 to 30 minutes. A travel listing gives hours of 5 am to 10 pm, with free entry.

namo-ghat.heading: Festivals and events at Namo Ghat
namo-ghat.body: Its open spaces have made Namo Ghat a venue for large public events. On Dev Deepawali in November 2025, the Chief Minister lit the first lamp here. The Ganga Mahotsav, UP Tourism's festival of music and dance, was staged at Raj Ghat and Namo Ghat from 1 to 4 November 2025. On 22, 24 and 25 October 2026 the Indian Air Force held an air show over the river at Namo Ghat, and the ghat was closed to the public for security on show and rehearsal days.

varanasi-ropeway.heading: The five stations and what they serve
varanasi-ropeway.body: The line runs from Varanasi Cantt, beside the railway station, to Kashi Vidyapith near the Bharat Mata Mandir, then Rathyatra and Girja Ghar (Church), and ends at Godowlia Chowk. Girja Ghar is a technical station where the line turns, and passengers will not board or leave there. From Godowlia it is a short walk to Dashashwamedh Ghat and the Kashi Vishwanath Dham. Rathyatra is the stop for Sigra, Lanka, BHU and Assi Ghat by auto or e-rickshaw. The ropeway does not go to Sarnath or the airport.

varanasi-ropeway.heading: Gondolas, capacity and cost
varanasi-ropeway.body: Recent reports describe 148 gondolas of 10 passengers each, with a cabin reaching each station about every two minutes. The design capacity is about 3,000 passengers an hour in each direction, and the line is planned to run about 16 hours a day. The cost was put at about ₹645 crore when the foundation stone was laid. The contract, including 15 years of operation and maintenance, is about ₹807–816 crore. It went to Vishwa Samudra Engineering with the Swiss ropeway maker Bartholet, whose engineers are supervising the work.

varanasi-ropeway.heading: Safety, luggage and accessibility
varanasi-ropeway.body: The system uses European-standard equipment, with sensors on the towers and a control room watching every cabin. It is set to stop automatically when wind speed goes above 60 km/h. If the power or main system fails, a backup can bring the gondolas to the nearest station. Stations have lifts and escalators, and wheelchair users can roll into the gondolas. Each passenger may carry up to 7 kg of luggage; more needs an extra ticket. A cloakroom at Cantt station is planned, free for ticket holders for the first two hours.

varanasi-ropeway.heading: Reported fares and passes
varanasi-ropeway.body: Amar Ujala reported in June 2026 that the state government had notified fares from ₹10 to ₹50: ₹50 for the full Cantt–Godowlia ride and ₹10 for the shortest hop, such as Vidyapith to Rathyatra. With the Kashi Smart Pass these fall to ₹40 and ₹8. Fares are to rise by 5% every 1 April. A premium gondola is listed at ₹2,000 a trip, and groups can reserve a whole gondola in advance for ₹1,200 a trip. Treat these as reported fares until the operator publishes its own fare table.

ganga-cruise.heading: MV Ganga Vilas: the long-distance cruise
ganga-cruise.body: The Ganga Vilas route covers about 3,200 km from Varanasi to Dibrugarh in Assam, passing through Bangladesh and across 27 river systems. The vessel has three decks and 18 suites for up to 36 tourists. Its itinerary was planned with visits to 50 tourist spots, including World Heritage Sites, national parks and cities such as Patna, Sahibganj, Kolkata, Dhaka and Guwahati. Thirty-two tourists from Switzerland signed up for the whole maiden voyage. For a short trip on the river in Varanasi itself, the day cruises are the practical choice.

ganga-cruise.heading: Day cruises past the 84 ghats
ganga-cruise.body: The city's Kashi Darshan portal lists cruise tours of the 84 ghats with audio commentary, on the double-decker Bhagirathi and the triple-decker Vivekanand/Manekshaw. Both have an air-conditioned lower deck and bio-toilets, and sell vegetarian snacks. The Alaknanda, run by Nordic Cruise Line, was listed in February 2025 with 9 am and 5:30 pm sailings of about 90 minutes from Ravidas Ghat, near Lanka, from ₹1,000 per person. The evening sailing includes the Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat. Check current times and fares with the operator.

ganga-cruise.heading: Timings, river levels and festival nights
ganga-cruise.body: In May 2024 the water police prohibited boating on the Ganga in Varanasi after 8:30 pm, citing tourist safety. When the river rises in the monsoon, boats are suspended. On 9 October 2026, after the water fell, large motorboats were allowed again from 6 am to 5 pm at half capacity, with life jackets compulsory, while rowing boats stayed banned. Cruises sell out early for Dev Deepawali: by 10 October 2026 the Alaknanda had been booked whole for ₹5 lakh, and the Sam Manekshaw was full at ₹15,000 per passenger.

ganga-cruise.heading: New vessels and planned terminals
ganga-cruise.body: In December 2025 India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell passenger vessel began commercial service from Namo Ghat. Built by Cochin Shipyard for the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), it is a 24-metre air-conditioned catamaran for 50 passengers. In November 2025 IWAI signed agreements with Heritage River Journeys and Alaknanda Cruises for new cruise vessels and premium river tourism in Varanasi and along the Ganga, worth more than ₹800 crore. It also announced two new river cruise terminals in Varanasi at a cost of ₹200 crore; no completion date was given.

rudraksh-convention-centre.heading: The building and its facilities
rudraksh-convention-centre.body: The centre stands on about 2.87 hectares in Sigra and cost about ₹186 crore, funded by Japan through JICA. Besides the main hall, which can be divided into smaller spaces, it has meeting rooms, a gallery with murals of Varanasi's culture, art and music, and parking for about 120 cars. It has a building management system and was built as an environment-friendly building fit for a level 3 GRIHA green rating. The building was designed to glow with LED lights at night.

rudraksh-convention-centre.heading: An India–Japan project
rudraksh-convention-centre.body: Former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe gifted the convention centre to the city during his visit to Varanasi in December 2015. In September 2017, at the India–Japan annual summit in Ahmedabad, it was named Rudraksh and its design was launched. The Japanese company Fujita Corporation built it. At the opening on 15 July 2021, Japan's Prime Minister Suga Yoshihide said in a video message that he hoped it would host international conferences and cultural and art events as a symbol of the friendship between the two countries.

rudraksh-convention-centre.heading: Events held here
rudraksh-convention-centre.body: The centre was built for conferences, exhibitions and concerts. In September 2023 it hosted the closing ceremony of the Kashi Sansad Sanskritik Mahotsav, where the Prime Minister gave prizes to the winners and launched registration for the Kashi Sansad Khel Pratiyogita. The sixth Sanskriti Sansad, a gathering on Indian culture organised by the Ganga Mahasabha with youth dialogues, exhibitions and a cultural festival, was scheduled here for 3 to 5 November 2026. Entry depends on the event, so check the organiser's details before going.

varanasi-cantt-station.heading: The station today
varanasi-cantt-station.body: Varanasi Junction, code BSB, is the city's main station and handles close to 300 trains a day, including Vande Bharat services. The station director said in April 2026 that about 94,000 people use it daily and that it earned about ₹743 crore in 2025–26, which keeps it in the railways' top NSG-1 category. Lifts, escalators, a restaurant, waiting rooms and a lounge are available. The state bus stand is just east of the station.

varanasi-cantt-station.heading: Yard remodelling in 2023
varanasi-cantt-station.body: Northern Railway remodelled the station yard in 45 days in 2023, after earlier plans of 120 and then 70 days. Afterwards the junction had 11 full-length platforms instead of three, and the railway said the yard could handle 80 to 100 pairs of trains a day without holding trains outside the station. During the work, from 20 September to 15 October 2023, the Vande Bharat and Mahanagari Express started from Banaras station instead, and several other trains were diverted.

varanasi-cantt-station.heading: What the redevelopment plans propose
varanasi-cantt-station.body: In April 2023 the Lucknow division's DRM said a new model of the station was ready and that a master plan and detailed project report would follow. The plan he described included a yoga and wellness centre, a mall, changes to the number and length of platforms, wider platforms 2 and 3, and lifts and escalators linked to the foot overbridges. The 2018 'world-class' plan listed CCTV, Wi-Fi, renovated station buildings, LED lighting, water ATMs and modular kiosks. Neither plan has a published completion date.

varanasi-cantt-station.heading: Arriving as a visitor
varanasi-cantt-station.body: An auto-rickshaw from the station to the riverfront cost about ₹100 in a 2023 listing. Many old-city lanes near the ghats are too narrow for cars and autos, so expect to walk the last stretch to Dashashwamedh Ghat and the Vishwanath Dham. The ropeway's Cantt terminus is being built beside the station, so arrivals will be able to ride to Godowlia once it opens. At peak times the railway adds crowd measures: for New Year 2026 it set up a holding area to protect passengers from the cold and posted medical teams.

banaras-station.heading: What the modernisation added
banaras-station.body: The RITES project built a new concourse with a large waiting area, circulating space, booking and reservation offices, a cafeteria, a food court and retiring rooms. Lifts and escalators were installed, the old station buildings were renovated, and CCTV cameras and LED lighting were added across the station. The area in front of the station was landscaped with fountains and seating. It was developed as a well-equipped station to ease the heavy rush at Varanasi Junction.

banaras-station.heading: From metre gauge to Banaras
banaras-station.body: The station opened in 1906 as a metre-gauge station on the Prayagraj–Mau–Gorakhpur line, which the Bengal and North Western Railway built between 1899 and 1913. It was converted to broad gauge in 1993–94. Today it belongs to the North Eastern Railway and is classed as an NSG-3 'Adarsh' station. Its new signboards show the name Banaras in Hindi, English, Urdu and Sanskrit.

banaras-station.heading: Trains that start here
banaras-station.body: Banaras is the terminus of several long-distance trains. The Shiv Ganga Express leaves New Delhi at 20:05 and reaches Banaras at 06:10 daily, and the Kashi Vishwanath Express also links Banaras with New Delhi. Other trains starting here include the Kashi Tamil Sangam Express to Kanyakumari, a Garib Rath to Anand Vihar in Delhi, and services to Pune, Mumbai's Lokmanya Tilak Terminus, Visakhapatnam and Patna. In autumn 2023, while Varanasi Junction's yard was rebuilt, the Vande Bharat and Mahanagari Express ran from here for several weeks.

banaras-station.heading: Getting to the ghats, and the next upgrade
banaras-station.body: From Banaras station, an auto-rickshaw to the riverfront cost about ₹100 in a 2023 listing; the old-city lanes near the ghats are too narrow for most vehicles, so the last stretch is on foot. Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, the North Eastern Railway listed Banaras in October 2024 among 58 stations being redeveloped, with about ₹53.33 crore earmarked for it. The scheme's plans cover station approach roads, waiting halls, toilets, lifts and escalators, free Wi-Fi, kiosks for local products, executive lounges and better passenger information.

varanasi-ring-road.heading: The three sections
varanasi-ring-road.body: Phase 1 is a 16.55 km four-lane road that links NH-56, the Lucknow highway, with NH-29 towards Ghazipur and Gorakhpur. It cost about ₹759 crore, includes two rail overbridges and a flyover, and was opened on 12 November 2018. The first package of Phase 2, from Rajatalab to Harhua, is a 16.98 km six-lane road that cost about ₹1,011 crore; the Kashi portal gives its inauguration as 25 October 2021. The second package runs about 27 km from Sandaha in Varanasi to Revasa in Chandauli district and cost about ₹949 crore. Newer central government documents number the ring road NH-135B.

varanasi-ring-road.heading: The bridge over the Ganga
varanasi-ring-road.body: The Ganga crossing is on the Sandaha–Revasa section. It runs from Babhanpura, near Chiraigaon on the Varanasi side, to Sultanpur village in Chandauli. Amar Ujala reported the bridge as about 1.8 km long and about 30 m high, so that floods do not stop traffic. At first only cars and two-wheelers could use the open carriageway; heavy vehicles were allowed later. In April 2026 they were barred again after repeated accidents, until the second carriageway is finished. From July to 30 September 2026 the stretch was also closed to all traffic every night, from 8 pm to 8 am, for bridge work.

varanasi-ring-road.heading: What it changes for travellers
varanasi-ring-road.body: Phase 1 took traffic on the Lucknow, Azamgarh and Gorakhpur highways around Varanasi instead of through it. The Harhua–Rajatalab stretch adds a bypass between the airport road and the Prayagraj highway. With the Ganga bridge, vehicles from Ghazipur, Ballia, Mau, Azamgarh, Jaunpur and Prayagraj bound for Bihar, Jharkhand or West Bengal no longer need to enter the city, and traffic between Ghazipur and Chandauli can skip it too. Amar Ujala estimated that about one lakh vehicles would avoid the city this way. This takes heavy through traffic off the city's roads.

varanasi-ring-road.heading: Delays and what is left
varanasi-ring-road.body: Building the Sandaha–Revasa section took about seven years. Zee News reported in 2025 that COVID-19, Ganga floods and the construction company's financial problems had slowed it, and that the deadline for the second carriageway had moved from 30 June to 31 December 2025. In July 2026 work on that carriageway was still going on, with the other side used for machinery and material. Four national highways meet the ring road: NH-19, NH-233, NH-56 and NH-29.

airport-expansion.heading: What the expansion includes
airport-expansion.body: The Cabinet approval raises the airport's capacity from 3.9 million to 9.9 million passengers a year. The new terminal is designed for 5,000 passengers in the busiest hour. The runway will be extended to 4,075 m by 45 m, and the new apron will hold 20 aircraft. The plan describes Varanasi as a green airport, with energy saving, waste recycling, solar power and natural daylight. At a review in June 2026, the terminal was described as having 72 check-in counters, eight aerobridges and multi-level car parking, with a design inspired by the Kashi Vishwanath temple.

airport-expansion.heading: A highway tunnel under the runway
airport-expansion.body: The runway is about 2,745 m long today. To make room for the extension, the national highway beside the airport (NH-31) is being realigned for 2.89 km and taken through a tunnel of about 450 m under the runway. News On AIR described it as the country's first six-lane underpass beneath an active runway. Swarajya reported that work began in September 2025, at an estimated cost of about ₹250 crore. In July 2026 the civil aviation minister said foundation and raft work was under way.

airport-expansion.heading: Background and milestones
airport-expansion.body: The Union Cabinet approved the project on 19 June 2024. On 20 October 2024 the Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for the runway expansion and the new terminal, described then as works worth about ₹2,870 crore. On 24 June 2026 the civil aviation minister reviewed the terminal and asked for it to be finished within six months; no opening date has been announced. The airport handled about 4.3 million passengers in 2025–26, already more than the 3.9 million a year cited as its capacity in 2024.

airport-expansion.heading: Using the airport in the meantime
airport-expansion.body: Flights use the existing terminal at Babatpur, on the Lucknow road north-west of the city. It has one lounge, Take Off Bar and Lounge, past security near Gate 2, open from 05:00 to 21:00. A prepaid taxi service works at the airport. A taxi or app cab to Godowlia Chowk, about 25 km away, costs about ₹600–1,000 and takes 45–75 minutes. Taxis usually stop there, and you walk or take a cycle rickshaw to the ghats. In December and January fog delays flights: on 6 January 2026, 26 flights were affected.

sarnath-redevelopment.heading: What the tourism works included
sarnath-redevelopment.body: The tourism project around the Buddhist sites cost about ₹90 crore, according to ETV Bharat, and was carried out by the Varanasi Development Authority under a World Bank-supported scheme. Besides streets, sewers and drainage, it covered façade lighting on the stupas, new signboards and electrical work, surface parking and a market area for food, handicrafts and One District One Product and GI-tagged goods. Plans published in 2023 focused on the area around the Dhamek and Chaukhandi stupas, where waterlogging had been a problem, and listed underground wiring, toilets, heritage-style street lights and Buddhist-themed signs.

sarnath-redevelopment.heading: What the UNESCO listing covers
sarnath-redevelopment.body: The World Heritage Committee inscribed the site at its 48th session, held in Busan, South Korea. The listing has two parts: the excavated remains of Sarnath, with the Dhamek and Dharmarajika stupas, and the Chaukhandi Stupa. Together they form the landscape known as the Deer Park, also called Rishipatana, Isipatana or Mrigadava. The core area is about 8 hectares, with a buffer zone of about 72 hectares. Sarnath had been on India's tentative list since 3 July 1998, and it is Uttar Pradesh's fourth World Heritage Site.

sarnath-redevelopment.heading: Building rules around the site
sarnath-redevelopment.body: No new construction is allowed within 100 m of the protected monuments. Between 100 m and 300 m, building or repair needs permission, and new buildings may not be taller than 9 m. The Varanasi Development Authority plans to check every building in the core and buffer zones, and its Sarnath team had issued 15 notices by early September 2026. Officials said existing homes are not at risk. Shopkeepers near the stupa told ETV Bharat they feared being moved but had not been contacted.

sarnath-redevelopment.heading: Visiting Sarnath now
sarnath-redevelopment.body: Sarnath is about 9–10 km from Varanasi Junction (Cantt), roughly 25–40 minutes by road. The ASI excavated site costs ₹20 online or ₹25 in cash for Indian, SAARC and BIMSTEC visitors, and ₹250 online or ₹300 in cash for other foreigners; children under 15 enter free. Chaukhandi Stupa has the same prices. The Sarnath Museum, which holds the Lion Capital of Ashoka, costs ₹5 and is closed on Fridays. Tickets can be booked on asi.paygov.org.in under Circle, then Sarnath.

kashi-tamil-sangamam.heading: Who takes part and how it is organised
kashi-tamil-sangamam.body: The programme is run by the Department of Higher Education in the Union Ministry of Education. Its partners are IIT Madras, Banaras Hindu University, the Central Institute of Classical Tamil in Chennai, the Uttar Pradesh government and several central ministries, including Culture, Railways and Tourism. For 2026, about 1,400 people from Tamil Nadu travel in seven groups of about 200. Each group's trip lasts eight days: four days of travel and four days of visits and programmes in Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya. Applications are taken only on kashitamil.iitm.ac.in.

kashi-tamil-sangamam.heading: The 2026 Thirukkural programme
kashi-tamil-sangamam.body: The 2026 theme is 'Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen' (Let us study the Thirukkural), the classical Tamil text on ethics. Thirukkural experts from Tamil Nadu will visit schools and colleges in Varanasi. The National Book Trust, with the Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya, will hold reading and storytelling sessions in Varanasi schools. A students' programme runs in 1,000 higher-education institutions across India, with details on kts.cict.in. As of early November 2026, the venues of the inauguration and the closing programme in Varanasi had not been announced.

kashi-tamil-sangamam.heading: What earlier editions looked like
kashi-tamil-sangamam.body: The first edition ran from 16 November to 15 December 2022, with more than 2,500 participants in 12 groups and daily cultural programmes at BHU. The second, from 17 to 30 December 2023, was held at Namo Ghat with 1,435 delegates; its exhibition of handlooms, crafts, books and food drew more than 2 lakh visitors. The third, from 15 to 24 February 2025, focused on Sage Agastya and took delegates to the Maha Kumbh at Prayagraj. In 2025 the plan was for 50 Tamil teachers to teach spoken Tamil to about 1,500 students in 50 Varanasi schools.

kashi-tamil-sangamam.heading: Tamil places in Kashi
kashi-tamil-sangamam.body: Delegations take a holy dip at Hanuman Ghat, earlier known as Rameswaram Ghat, and visit the poet Subramania Bharati's residence there. The area around the ghat has South Indian maths, including the Kanchi, Kerala, Sankara and Sringeri maths. Tours have also covered the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Kedar Ghat and Sarnath. In 2022, the 75 stalls of handloom, crafts, clothing and North and South Indian food at the BHU Amphitheatre were open to local people as well as delegates. Visitors in Varanasi at Sangamam time can see these places on their own.

ganjari-cricket-stadium.heading: What is being built
ganjari-cricket-stadium.body: The stadium covers about 30.6 acres. The Uttar Pradesh government acquired the land for about ₹121 crore and is to lease it to the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA), which funds construction with BCCI support; building was estimated at about ₹330 crore. In August 2023 UPCA gave Larsen & Toubro a design-and-build contract. The plan covers an ICC-standard main ground, a practice ground, floodlights, a display scoreboard, corporate boxes, VIP lounges, broadcasting booths and press conference rooms. The stands are stepped like the ghats, and the façade sheets are shaped like bilva leaves.

ganjari-cricket-stadium.heading: Where it is
ganjari-cricket-stadium.body: The site is outside Ganjari village in Raja Talab tehsil, about 15 km from Varanasi, beside Phase 2 of the Varanasi Ring Road. It is the third international cricket stadium in Uttar Pradesh, after Green Park in Kanpur and Ekana in Lucknow, and the first in the Purvanchal region. Varanasi's two older stadiums each sit on about 15 acres. The new ground is built for day-night matches.

ganjari-cricket-stadium.heading: Progress so far
ganjari-cricket-stadium.body: Aaj Tak reported the work about 75% complete in December 2025. At the District Magistrate's inspection on 16 August 2026, the project officer said the 'damru' structure was the only major item left, due by 15 October, and that the rest of the external works would be finished in September. In early November 2026 the district administration sent a progress report on the stadium to the Prime Minister's Office.

ganjari-cricket-stadium.heading: Before matches can be played
ganjari-cricket-stadium.body: International and domestic matches can be scheduled only after BCCI approves the ground. A BCCI team is to inspect the pitch, the quality of play and the facilities for players and spectators. In September 2026 Amar Ujala reported that a Ranji Trophy match could be the first test of the new pitch and outfield, if everything met the standards. Under-19 matches and Women's Premier League games have been discussed, but no fixture had been confirmed as of early November 2026.

heritage-corridors-parks.heading: Parks and food-street hubs
heritage-corridors-parks.body: The larger MoU, worth about ₹48 crore, covers 119 public parks across Varanasi. Planned work includes landscaping, walking paths, open gyms, children's play equipment, drainage, lighting and planting. The same MoU pays for two food-street hubs, at Sarnath and Maidagin, with organised vending in place of scattered stalls, water and sanitation, CCTV, solar lighting and visitor facilities. BPCL is carrying it out with the Kashi Integrated Parking and Recreational Foundation (KIPRF) and Varanasi Smart City Limited.

heritage-corridors-parks.heading: Heritage routes in the old city
heritage-corridors-parks.body: The second MoU, about ₹21.21 crore, is with the Varanasi Development Authority. It covers three stretches: the Thatheri heritage lane to the Kaal Bhairav temple, the building façades from Godowlia crossing to Maidagin crossing, and the lane leading to the Manikarnikeshwar temple at Manikarnika Ghat. Planned work includes heritage-style roads with stone paving, façade repair, heritage lighting, signs, street furniture, murals and public art, and more room for people on foot.

heritage-corridors-parks.heading: Where these routes are
heritage-corridors-parks.body: All three stretches lie on walks many visitors already take. Taxis often drop passengers at Godowlia Chowk for the ghats, and the façade work runs from there to Maidagin crossing. The Kaal Bhairav temple stands near the Head Post Office in Visheshwarganj. Its present building dates from the mid-17th century, and Bhairav is believed to be the kotwal, the protector of the city. The third lane leads down to Manikarnika, the main cremation ghat.

heritage-corridors-parks.heading: Background
heritage-corridors-parks.body: Both MoUs were signed on 7 September 2026 at the Taj hotel in Nadesar, with Varanasi's mayor, the divisional commissioner and BPCL's chairman and managing director present. The money comes from Bharat Petroleum's corporate social responsibility (CSR) budget, and each project has 36 months for completion. Neither MoU, as reported, names individual parks, and the number of stalls at the food-street hubs has not been published.

highway-package-2026.heading: The Varuna corridor
highway-package-2026.body: The Varuna corridor runs 43.218 km between NH-31 and the ring road, mostly on an elevated 6/4-lane road with flyovers, loops, ramps and service roads. Of its ₹10,998.32 crore cost, about ₹4,565 crore is for civil construction and about ₹935 crore for land. It is designed for 80–100 km/h. The government expects it to cut the trip between NH-31 and Kashi Railway Station from about 40 minutes to 20, and to improve access to the airport, Varanasi Junction, Varanasi City station, Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction, Ramnagar port and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

highway-package-2026.heading: The Ganga corridor
highway-package-2026.body: The Ganga corridor is a 46.039 km six-lane elevated road between NH-19 and the ring road, which is numbered NH-135B. It includes a 910 m cable-stayed bridge across the Ganga and a 1.32 km extradosed footbridge with travelators, giving people on foot a link to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. A rail overbridge will cross the existing and proposed Malviya Bridge, and an elevated spur between BHU/Lanka and Samne Ghat is meant to relieve Lanka junction. Civil construction is costed at about ₹6,038 crore and land at about ₹541 crore.

highway-package-2026.heading: What it would change for visitors
highway-package-2026.body: The government says average travel times in the area served by the Ganga corridor would fall from about 60 minutes to 20, and NH-19 to Kashi Railway Station from about 50 minutes to 25. The corridor is planned to link the airport, the Kashi, Banaras and Varanasi City stations and the Ramnagar port with Kashi Vishwanath, BHU, Namo Ghat, Ramnagar Fort and the ghats. It would also take through traffic off NH-19, the BHU–Ramnagar road and NH-35. Both projects are part of the Varanasi Decongestion Plan.

highway-package-2026.heading: Status and land acquisition
highway-package-2026.body: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved both projects on 15 July 2026. Before that, on 18 June 2026, and again on 10 July, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways named the Additional District Magistrate (East), Varanasi, as the competent authority for land acquisition on the first 19.42 km of the Varuna corridor. The notices list villages in Pindra and Sadar tehsils. No construction start date has been announced.
